API-1.statement: Headless core. Check: the core starts with no screen; the runner keeps running and `orch` commands fall back to the files when the core dies.

API-10.statement: Files stay canonical. Check: deleting the core's cache and restarting gives identical answers; records survive a restart.

API-11.statement: Ordered events. Check: events have a gap-free increasing seq and the envelope {seq, ts, kind, data, v}.

API-12.statement: Resume. Check: `events.subscribe from_seq` replays exactly the missed events; an expired cursor returns cursor_expired with a snapshot.

API-13.statement: Filtering and bounds. Check: a kind filter works; a slow subscriber is dropped without delaying others or the writer.

API-14.statement: Events carry no secrets. Check: events hold ids and summaries only; a planted secret and transcript text never appear.

API-15.statement: Records-first answers. Check: canned questions (status, usage, CI, versions, history, why stopped) are answered from records with sources, as_of and tokens_used 0, and nothing is written to the inbox.

API-16.statement: Forwarding at safe points. Check: a judgment question is queued only in the inbox, delivered at a safe point as at most 300 tokens with a TTL; query.reply produces query.answered for the asker.

API-17.statement: Talk is labelled and capped. Check: context.push is labelled by source, capped (2 KB, 10 per minute), delivered as quoted untrusted data, and never counted as an owner decision.

API-18.statement: Tokens. Check: 256-bit, stored hashed, revocable, minted only at the owner's terminal (refused over the API); an agent token defaults to read plus context.push.

API-19.statement: Scope matrix. Check: read, confirm and owner scopes each allow exactly their methods; others return forbidden.

API-2.statement: Socket. Check: socket mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, path under 104 bytes, a stale socket is replaced, no TCP listener.

API-20.statement: Decisions. Check: decision.answer works for the owner role only.

API-21.statement: Two-step confirm. Check: a control call first returns confirm_required with an id; the second call within 60 s executes once; reuse, expiry and a different token or params are refused.

API-22.statement: Owner-only wall. Check: install, update, setup, reviewed install, live-record writes, billing attestation, client-range widening and token minting are refused over the API even with an owner token.

API-23.statement: Audit. Check: every change and confirm is a commands.jsonl line; every refusal is an audit.jsonl line (rotated separately, so refusals cannot push changes out); each line has caller, method, outcome; no token or secret appears.

API-24.statement: Limits. Check: request size, string length, method time, connection count and subscription count are capped with fixed error codes.

API-25.statement: Provider neutrality. Check: no provider name in method, event or field names; provider detail only under `extra`.

API-26.statement: (later adapter) HTTP+SSE bridge on 127.0.0.1 with Host/Origin/token checks, SSE id = seq. Tested with the dashboard milestone.

API-27.statement: (later adapter) stdio MCP adapter on a pinned spec exposing the same operations. Tested last.

API-3.statement: Peer identity. Check: a connection from another uid is refused before any method runs.

API-4.statement: Framing. Check: JSON-RPC 2.0 as newline-delimited JSON; a malformed line gets a parse error and the connection lives; an oversize line is refused.

API-5.statement: Handshake and versioning. Check: `initialize` returns protocol version and features; a major mismatch is refused; any other method before it is refused.

API-6.statement: One contract. Check: `schema.get` lists methods, event kinds and error codes; every response carries `seq_at`; the in-process adapter and the socket give identical results.

API-7.statement: State, units and runs. Check: state.get, units.list/get/history and runs.list equal the record files field for field.

API-8.statement: Usage, history, CI, versions. Check: values equal the records; unreadable or missing data is "unknown", never a guessed number.

API-9.statement: Health. Check: health.get gives each finding with a plain reason code and text.

B2-OUTCOME.statement:
**B2-OUTCOME — The project service records a finished child's outcome itself.**
A committed terminal whose orchestration is still open (active or paused), whose reservation is live, whose context is
`committed` and whose run belongs to the writer's own runtime and host class is recorded by the service on its own
writer, right after the result is safely stored and again by a bounded, fair sweep after a restart. The outcome is a
pure function of the store: the service's and the primary's records are byte-identical. One final predicate
(`ServiceRecordAuthority`, a required typed check) runs as the first statement of the admission transaction at the
service entry and at the primary's, so admission, close, interruption, the 24 h idle end and expiry meet at one
boundary; after any of those nothing new is recorded and "unrecorded" is final (owner decision 92.1 A). The primary's
later call on a recorded run is a read-only retrieval that writes nothing, works after a normal close, and never
changes who recorded it; its refusals are named and write nothing. Who recorded (`service` or `primary`) lives in a
small separate table keyed by the receipt id with no foreign key (schema step 19 -> 20, owner decision 92.3 A);
receipts, records and the enrolled operation set are unchanged; the service entry has no socket entry; the service
writes no QA and never sets `accepted`.
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-B2-outcome.md draft 2 with the s2 corrections, rows B2-1 to B2-18; owner decision 92; docs/requirements/b2.md.

E1-1.statement: **E1-1 — Consent first.** RS-11, decision 90.11 A. Setup asks once, in plain words with the real reason, with a pick-list (yes / not now) and a details view, before the collector gets a login-start entry. Nothing is written or run without a yes; not now writes and runs nothing; a failed install is reported and not remembered. Tests: tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_1_asks_once_with_reason_pick_list_and_details_and_installs_only_on_yes, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_1_a_failed_install_is_reported_and_not_remembered.

E1-10.statement: **E1-10 — The entry's command passes the runtime check.** The command the rendered entry holds (launchd ProgramArguments, systemd ExecStart), run as given, reaches require_authorized_collector_runtime and starts only when the state's authorized runtime is the installed one; with a different authorized digest it is refused with runtime_unauthorized. The CLI prints the refusal's message, not its code, so the run's printed refusal is matched to the message the collector's own check raises with that code. Tests: tests.test_login_start.CommandAuthorizationTests.test_E1_10_the_rendered_command_passes_require_authorized_collector_runtime, tests.test_login_start.CommandAuthorizationTests.test_E1_10_the_installed_command_run_as_given_is_refused_with_runtime_unauthorized (the rendered launchd command run as a real process against a temporary installed copy). The real launchd and systemd back-off on a real install stays an owner check.

E1-2.statement: **E1-2 — macOS entry.** A launchd user agent in the account's LaunchAgents folder runs the installed collector command (absolute paths, isolated Python, learning-serve) at login, restarts it after a crash with a throttle (KeepAlive on failure, ThrottleInterval), logs to the CoCoLo log folder, and holds no secret. Loaded through an injected runner (launchctl bootstrap), never the real one in tests. Test: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_2_launchd_plist_and_load.

E1-3.statement: **E1-3 — Linux entry.** A systemd user unit runs the same command, with Restart=on-failure, RestartSec and StartLimit back-off, logs to the CoCoLo log folder, WantedBy=default.target, and no secret; enabled through the injected runner (systemctl --user). Test: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_3_systemd_unit_and_enable.

E1-4.statement: **E1-4 — Ask once.** The answer (yes or no) is kept in the private installer folder beside the project list. A re-run of setup does not ask again; with no private place to keep the answer, setup does not ask and says so; an update never asks. Tests: tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_4_answered_is_not_asked_again, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_4_no_place_to_keep_the_answer_means_no_question, tests.test_login_start.AnswerTests.test_E1_4_answer_round_trip_and_refusals.

E1-5.statement: **E1-5 — Removal.** Removing unloads the entry through the runner, deletes its file, records no, and works when the file is already gone or the unload fails. Offered under Configure when the entry is on. Tests: tests.test_login_start.RemoveTests.test_E1_5_remove_unloads_and_deletes, tests.test_login_start.RemoveTests.test_E1_5_remove_tolerates_missing_file_and_failed_unload, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_5_configure_offers_remove_when_on_and_turn_on_when_off.

E1-6.statement: **E1-6 — Refusals.** A relative command path, a symlinked entry path, an existing entry that is another user's or that others can change, or an unsupported system is refused with a plain reason and changes nothing; the entry is written through folder descriptors opened without following a link. Tests: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_6_refusals_change_nothing, tests.test_login_start.OfferTests.test_E1_6_unsupported_system_is_not_asked, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_6_an_entry_another_user_owns_or_others_can_change_is_not_replaced.

E1-7.statement: **E1-7 — Wired into setup.** The collector step offers login start after the collector is ready, in setup (an update never asks), through the audited terminal runner; the existing Configure menu is unchanged. Test: tests.test_login_start.WiringTests.test_E1_7_setup_offers_login_start_after_the_collector_is_ready.

E1-8.statement: **E1-8 — Status reports the entry.** Setup's status lines report the login entry as on, off or stale. Stale means the entry's command no longer matches the installed collector's path, or the installed runtime's identity (the digest the owner authorized) is not the one the entry was last written for, or that identity cannot be read. The entry is read only through folder descriptors opened without following a link, never blocking on a FIFO or device, and only when it is the owner's and others cannot change it; otherwise it is stale. A status line holds no private value: no digest, key or folder path; its reason is one of a fixed set. Tests: tests.test_login_start.StatusTests.test_E1_8_status_is_on_off_or_stale_and_names_no_private_value, tests.test_login_start.StatusTests.test_E1_8_the_runtime_identity_is_read_only_from_a_private_plain_authorization_file, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_8_status_never_follows_a_link_or_blocks_on_a_special_file_or_reads_another_users_entry.

E1-9.statement: **E1-9 — An update keeps the entry current.** When consent is already recorded (E1-4: an update never asks), an update that changes the collector's path or the authorized runtime digest rewrites the existing entry through the runner and records what it was written for; when it cannot, the entry is reported stale with a plain reason and the earlier entry is kept. The authorized runtime is the one the collector's own active-identity check (require_authorized_collector_runtime: exact schema, not quiesced, owner-only, never through a link) accepts for this setup's attested runtime; any other is reported stale and nothing is written. An update never asks and never creates an entry, whatever its answers file says. The record and the answer are read only from owner-only plain files of the owner's, never through a link or blocking. A failure shows a fixed reason with no path; when the record cannot be kept the earlier entry is put back and the entry is not shown as refreshed. An entry that is current is not rewritten; with no recorded yes, or with no entry, nothing is written. Tests: tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_9_a_failed_refresh_puts_a_stopped_systemd_unit_back_stopped_and_not_enabled, tests.test_login_start.InstallTests.test_E1_9_a_refresh_does_not_recreate_an_entry_that_vanished, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_a_rewrite_needs_the_collectors_active_identity_for_the_attested_runtime, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_the_runtime_record_and_the_answer_are_read_only_from_private_plain_files_of_this_user, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_an_update_never_creates_an_entry_from_an_answers_file, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_a_failed_rewrite_shows_a_fixed_reason_with_no_path, tests.test_login_start.ReviewFixTests.test_E1_9_a_failed_record_write_keeps_the_earlier_entry_and_is_not_shown_as_refreshed, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_an_update_that_moves_the_collector_rewrites_the_entry_without_asking, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_an_update_that_changes_the_runtime_digest_rewrites_the_entry, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_an_entry_that_cannot_be_rewritten_is_reported_stale_with_a_reason, tests.test_login_start.UpgradeTests.test_E1_9_a_current_entry_a_missing_entry_and_no_consent_write_nothing.

E1-WS.statement: **E1-WS — Wizard source safety.** The Python setup wizard keeps the source-level safety properties setup.sh's source tests checked (audited launch builders, literal non-porcelain git with the trusted binary and helpers off, isolated Python, provider clients never run by name, product naming and screen wording). Source: tests/test_setup_wizard_source.py module docstring (S5) and owner decision 112b A (2026-11-24).

E1a-T2.statement:
After earlier phases succeed, a different thread must actually hold the ledger
lock during claim/open completion, stale-input recapture, initial open
authorization and both provenance adapters. The decoded reply must give exactly
`account_busy` (or `open_account_busy` for open), with the exact plain next step
“The account's records were busy: try again in a moment.” Contention must leave
the lane unfaulted with no failure note. Releasing the holder must allow a
successful retry. Enrollment can be synthetic, but the initial-open authorizer
and the contended ledger operations must be real.

E1a-T3.statement:
Real `AccountService.handle` and `begin` entries give successive waits one
request budget. A deferred open publication exhausts its own budget; the next
request and owner pump must observe a fresh budget. A collector frame received
slowly starts its ledger budget only after receipt, and the next frame gets a
fresh budget. A frame whose dispatch raises must also restore the request
deadline on the same thread, allowing the next frame a fresh budget. A controlled
clock may advance time without sleeping; actual ledger operations remain wired in.

E1a-T4.statement:
Use events/barriers, rather than a timed load loop, to coordinate simultaneous
refusals through the held, write-unit, account-transaction, read-call, reader
entry, slot-health, sweep and project-health acquisition paths. Assert the exact
whole per-label count dictionary while ledger-free health reads run concurrently.
All workers must acknowledge completion, and release must permit ordinary work.

E1b-1.statement: One opening thread constructs the ledger and account views and executes every SQL statement through shutdown.

E1b-2.statement: Whole ledger operations including account transactions and their authority rechecks execute as one owner request.

E1b-3.statement: The standalone ledger owner queue bounds queued and running custody through completion, including abandonment and expiry, schedules projects fairly, and immediately returns named, counted existing busy refusals on overflow. Queue limits are configurable; decision 304 fixes measured defaults at 12 retained requests, 8 projects, 6 per project and an 800 ms wait.

E1b-4.statement: A caller waits only until the earlier of its absolute deadline and the configured maximum of 800 ms. Expired queued work is skipped; running work completes whole, retains custody until handled, and answers busy after its deadline.

E1b-5.statement: Operation Exceptions become plain operation_rejected error results without sharing exception objects or tracebacks; the owner continues serving. KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit remain on the owner thread and requests are acknowledged.

E1b-6.statement: Close stops admission immediately with a counted closed cause and an existing caller busy reason, finishes running work whole, then refuses and acknowledges queued work and releases custody. Close is idempotent and nonblocking; drain has a finite timeout.

E1b-7.statement: Accepted requests provide a handled acknowledgement after owner execution or skipping, outcome publication and custody release. Unit tests coordinate on events and controlled clocks without sleeps or timed polling.

E1b-8.statement: Preparation runs before owner requests where existing checks permit, and current authority is rechecked before commit.

E2ELEAK-1.statement: **E2ELEAK-1 — Every World ends cleanly.** After pass, assertion failure, exception, step timeout, partial construction failure, interpreter exit or SIGTERM, every process started by that World is stopped and its e2e directory is removed. Detached collectors, project services and clients are included. Cleanup is idempotent and bounded.

E2ELEAK-2.statement: **E2ELEAK-2 — Safe recorded ownership.** Persist World identity and process pid plus operating-system start time before running product code. Only matching records belonging to that World may be signalled; pid reuse, another World, malformed records and unrecorded lookalikes must never select a process. No process-name scan is permitted.

E2ELEAK-3.statement: **E2ELEAK-3 — Drained stop before escalation.** Teardown first requests the collector's own shutdown_if_drained operation using the World's installed runtime and socket, without starting a collector. Then signal matching recorded survivors with SIGTERM and finally SIGKILL, verifying exit before removing the World directory. Registration closes during teardown so a late child cannot escape.

E2ELEAK-4.statement: **E2ELEAK-4 — Runner recovery owns recorded detached processes.** Each worker records its Worlds in its assigned runner folder. On completion, failure, timeout or runner SIGTERM/interruption, the runner reaps these recorded Worlds as well as its worker group, including detached processes outside TMPDIR. A World guardian also handles abrupt owner death. Discovery never scans other e2e directories or touches pre-existing leaked processes. If both runner and guardian are SIGKILLed, or the machine reboots, no next-run scan recovers them; surviving processes and directories require a manual sweep.

E2a-1.statement:
**E2a-1 — Additive ledger schema.** (D:21, D:35, D:40, D:127) Opening the collector ledger adds, without changing
`PRAGMA user_version` (16), the nullable columns `launch_copy` and `launch_digest` to `projects` and the table
`project_wake` (one row per project: allocated epoch, published generation epoch + seq, state
`pending|exact|clean_stop` or null when only reconciled, next due, a body digest, the collector's `due_at_ms`, a
refused count, the update time) with an index on `due_at_ms` for due rows. Reopening is idempotent. The launch columns are
machine-local: a project backup snapshot keeps its exact earlier format (the six original project columns) and a
restored row has no launch record. Tests: tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LedgerSchemaTests.test_E2a_1_additive_columns_and_wake_table_keep_the_schema_version,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LedgerSchemaTests.test_E2a_1_backup_keeps_its_format_and_restore_has_no_launch_record.
Review round 1: also the additive table `project_wake_instances` (per project, the service instance its last epoch was allocated to; machine-local, never in a backup).

E2a-10.statement:
**E2a-10 — Setup records the launch target for every project.** (primary decision 171) The setup and update
registration step (`learning-register`, which Codex and Claude-only setups alike run) installs the project's protected
runtime copy, validates it as the launch target (E2a-3) and records it through the running collector, then marks it
registered (E2a-4); no Codex rule is written. It reports `launch_record: recorded` or `not_recorded`; a failure never
fails the registration. `install-codex-rule` keeps recording too. Test:
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.SetupRecordTests.test_E2a_10_registration_records_the_launch_target_without_the_codex_rule.

E2a-11.statement:
**E2a-11 — Status for a project with no launch record.** (primary decision 171) `learning-status` shows `recovery:
"recovery pending: run setup to record the install"` for a registered project whose collector row has no launch record
(never recorded, or restored from a backup, which excludes the machine-local launch columns), and null when the record
exists. Test: tests.test_e2a_launch_record.SetupRecordTests.test_E2a_11_status_says_run_setup_when_no_launch_record_exists,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LaunchAuthorityTests.test_E2a_11_launch_status_authorizes_its_subject_before_any_lookup.
Review round 1: `launch_status` answers only an owner-signed request (as `record_launch`), checked before any lookup; an unsigned request gets the same refusal for every root. A caller who cannot sign (no line) shows null.

E2a-2.statement:
**E2a-2 — Registration never writes the launch record.** (D:24, D:127) The registration insert names its columns
explicitly; a newly registered project has a null `launch_copy`, `launch_digest` and no wake row. Test:
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LedgerSchemaTests.test_E2a_2_registration_names_its_columns_and_writes_no_launch_record.

E2a-3.statement:
**E2a-3 — Setup writes a validated launch record.** (D:21-23, D:113-114) `install-codex-rule` (the setup step that
writes the protected copy) validates the launch target and then records `launch_copy` + `launch_digest` for the
project's active row. The target is valid only when the copy sits at
`~/.codex/agent-orchestration/<project digest>/<runtime digest>`, its name is the digest, its binding names this
project and `runtime_copy_problem(copy, root)` is None; where setup ran (`clone_root`) is not consulted. The ledger
refuses a record whose digest is not 64 hex, whose copy is not absolute, or whose copy's name is not the digest or
whose parent is not the project's digest folder, and an unregistered project; a refusal changes nothing. The record goes
through the running collector's new mutating `record_launch` operation (RS-F S1 runtime gate) or, with no collector
running, the ledger directly. Tests: tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LaunchTargetTests.test_E2a_3_a_valid_copy_is_a_launch_target_whatever_clone_ran_setup,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LaunchTargetTests.test_E2a_3_a_copy_bound_elsewhere_or_changed_is_not_a_launch_target,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LedgerSchemaTests.test_E2a_3_ledger_records_only_a_well_formed_launch_record,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.CollectorRecordTests.test_E2a_3_record_launch_over_the_collector_wire_and_its_runtime_gate,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LaunchTargetTests.test_E2a_3_setup_records_the_launch_target_through_the_collector,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.LaunchAuthorityTests.test_E2a_3_record_launch_needs_the_owner_and_a_copy_the_collector_verifies,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.SetupOfflineTests.test_E2a_3_with_no_collector_running_setup_records_in_the_ledger.
Review round 1: `record_launch` is the owner's only: the request carries an `owner-cli-v1` preamble under the key the collector issues at each start (`<state>/collector-owner/owner.cap`, proof written in its owner-only proof folder) naming exactly this request with the project root as subject, checked before anything else; then the collector itself verifies the whole target with `launch_target_problem` (its trusted copy root: the account's `~/.codex/agent-orchestration/<project digest>/<digest>`, bound to this project, byte for byte); any failure is `operation_rejected` and changes nothing. With no collector answering at all, setup records directly in the ledger under exclusive owner maintenance (`CollectorMaintenance`); a collector of another runtime is never stopped for it (`not_recorded`).
Decision 179: the owner proof's wrong key and a replayed proof are refused over the collector wire for both `record_launch` and `launch_status` (tests.test_e2a_launch_record.FinalWireTests.test_E2a_3_record_launch_and_launch_status_refuse_a_wrong_key_and_a_replayed_proof).

E2a-4.statement:
**E2a-4 — Copy pinning.** (D:115-116) The registered copy (marked by setup once its launch record is written; one per
project) and any copy held in use (`pin_runtime_copy`, a shared lock a launcher holds from verification until its child
serves) are pinned. `prune_runtime_copies` skips pinned copies; a same-name replacement of a copy in use is refused and
leaves it in place; owner removal leaves an in-use copy in place (and reports no container removed) and otherwise removes
as before. A launcher cannot pin a copy while a prune, replacement or removal holds it. Tests:
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinningTests.test_E2a_4_prune_skips_the_registered_and_in_use_copies,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinningTests.test_E2a_4_replacement_and_removal_skip_a_copy_in_use,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinningTests.test_E2a_4_a_pin_waits_for_no_one_and_fails_while_a_prune_holds_the_copy,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinOrderTests.test_E2a_4_setup_pins_the_new_copy_before_the_record_and_clears_the_old_pin_after,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinOrderTests.test_E2a_4_a_copy_pinned_while_a_prune_runs_is_never_removed,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinOrderTests.test_E2a_4_a_pin_on_a_lock_file_a_replacement_dropped_never_lets_a_second_replacement_in,
tests.test_e2a_launch_record.PinOrderTests.test_E2a_4_owner_removal_keeps_the_registered_copy.
Review round 1: the project's stable lock (its copies' folder, flocked exclusive) serializes prune, replacement, removal and the registered marks; a launcher's shared pin checks the lock file it locked is the one the path names (a dropped lock file is never a pin). Setup marks the new copy before its record commits and drops the earlier mark only after; a failed record keeps the earlier mark and drops only one it added; a mark is refused for a copy already gone. Owner removal also leaves the registered copy (and its folder) in place.
Decision 179: setup holds the project lock from its mark through the record to its cleanup, so concurrent setups take turns and none clears the mark of the record that won; setup never replaces the registered copy while it verifies (only where setup ran would differ); a record whose outcome is unknown (the collector exchange failed after delivery: transport failure, unreadable or oversized reply) keeps both marks until the next record that succeeds. Tests: tests.test_e2a_launch_record.FinalFixTests.test_E2a_4_concurrent_setups_never_clear_the_mark_of_the_record_that_won, tests.test_e2a_launch_record.FinalFixTests.test_E2a_4_setup_never_replaces_the_registered_copy_that_verifies, tests.test_e2a_launch_record.FinalFixTests.test_E2a_4_a_lost_record_reply_keeps_the_new_copy_pinned.

E2a-5.statement:
**E2a-5 — Publish credential bound to one project.** (D:31-33, D:117-118) `account.publish_wake` is a
PROJECT_OPERATIONS operation. Its credential is a per-project wake key (`client-runtimes/<root digest>.wake.cap`), issued
by the collector for every active project at account-host start and at registration. The verifier picks the key by
the preamble's subject: a `project` preamble whose MAC verifies only under that subject's wake key is marked bound to it;
such a credential may call `account.publish_wake` and nothing else, and `account.publish_wake` is refused for any other
credential. A key for project A presented for B's root, an unknown root, a forged body or a replayed preamble is
refused at enrollment exactly as for an unknown project; a bound credential whose body names another project id, a known
or an unknown one, gets the same `account_not_authorized` before any lookup of the target's wake state; nothing changes.
Tests: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeWireTests.test_E2a_5_a_credential_is_bound_to_one_project_and_denials_are_uniform,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeWireTests.test_E2a_5_the_wake_key_publishes_nothing_else_and_the_account_key_cannot_publish,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_5_the_verifier_probes_no_caller_named_path_and_binds_the_project_id.
Review round 1: the verifier's keys are an in-memory table filled where the keys are issued (account-host start, registration), each bound to the immutable project id it was issued for; a subject with no key is checked against a dummy key, and no caller-named path is touched; a bound credential is authorized by that id alone (no root lookup).

E2a-6.statement:
**E2a-6 — Generations: durable epoch, seq, idempotent, stale refused.** (D:34-36, D:121-122) The payload is exactly
`epoch` (null, or an allocated epoch), `seq` (>= 1), `state` and `next_due_at_ms` (null or >= 0). A null epoch allocates
the project's next epoch, durably and strictly increasing across collector restarts. A strictly newer (epoch, seq)
replaces the row; the same generation with the same body is `duplicate` and changes nothing; an older generation, the
same generation with a different body, or an epoch never allocated is refused `wake_stale`, counted, the row otherwise
unchanged. The reply is exactly `{epoch, seq, outcome}`; the new operation is in the B4m reply-shape table, and the
RS-F S1 gate refuses it from another runtime with `runtime_upgrade_required` before authorization, changing nothing.
Tests: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeWireTests.test_E2a_6_epochs_are_durable_duplicates_are_no_ops_and_stale_is_refused,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeLedgerTests.test_E2a_6_ledger_generation_rules,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeProtocolTests.test_E2a_6_reply_shape_row_and_closed_reply,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeProtocolTests.test_E2a_6_runtime_gate_refuses_an_old_caller_before_authorization,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_6_a_lost_first_acknowledgement_does_not_allocate_a_second_epoch.
Review round 1: a null-epoch payload may also carry `instance` (32 hex, fresh per service instance, MAC-bound); a retry from the instance the last epoch was allocated to gets that epoch again, not a new one.
Decision 179: epochs are per instance (`project_wake_instances` keyed by project and instance): an older instance retrying after its successor gets its own older epoch (stale once the successor published), never a newer one; a row goes once its instance publishes with its epoch. Test: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_6_an_older_instance_retrying_after_its_successor_never_supersedes_it.

E2a-7.statement:
**E2a-7 — Crash-safe wake from the project service.** (D:37-39, D:119-120) A project service, once its store is open,
publishes `pending` (allocating its epoch) and then `exact` with its store's next due (the earliest `due_at_ms` of a
held or releasing hold). Before any hold write (`take_hold`, or a custody deadline being set) whose deadline is earlier than
the last acknowledged publication's, or before its first hold write while this instance has no acknowledged
publication, it publishes `pending` and waits for the acknowledgement, at most 2 s. After the transaction ends it
publishes `exact` with the next due, from a background sender, never overtaking a later `pending`. With the collector
unreachable the write proceeds and the instance keeps an unpublished flag and retries. Killed between the pending
acknowledgement and the commit, or between the commit and `exact`, the ledger keeps `pending` (unknown, E2a-9).
Tests: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeServiceTests.test_E2a_7_a_live_service_publishes_pending_then_exact,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeServiceTests.test_E2a_7_killed_after_the_pending_ack_or_after_commit_leaves_pending,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakePublisherTests.test_E2a_7_earlier_deadlines_need_a_pending_ack_and_exact_never_overtakes_it,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakePublisherTests.test_E2a_7_unreachable_collector_lets_the_write_proceed_flagged,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_7_a_first_write_unpublished_after_a_clean_stop_is_still_reconciled,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_7_a_write_while_pending_invalidates_the_queued_exact,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_7_a_releasing_open_binding_counts_by_its_withdrawal_retry,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_7_a_reply_past_the_limit_is_refused_and_flagged.
Review round 1: (a) a first write with no acknowledged publication (the collector may still hold `clean_stop`) first leaves the durable marker `<state>/projects/<id>/wake-unpublished`, which reconcile reads, and is refused (`history_service_unavailable`) when even that cannot be written; the first acknowledged publication removes it. (b) every hold write invalidates a queued `exact`. (c) the next due also counts a releasing open binding's withdrawal retry (`next_check_ms`), and marking a withdrawal (which moves it earlier) is guarded like `take_hold`. A reply past 16 KiB ends the exchange (flagged, retried).
Decision 179: (a) the marker is a folder `wake-unpublished/` of one file per instance (named by it, created under a dot name, flocked for the instance's life, then renamed into place); an acknowledgement removes its own and those whose lock is free (instance gone), never a live overlapping instance's. (b) `touch()` invalidates a queued `exact` too. (c) a withdrawal deferral's retry goes through the same guard as `take_hold` (it may move earlier). Tests: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_7_an_overlapping_publisher_s_acknowledgement_keeps_the_other_s_marker, tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_7_a_touch_invalidates_the_queued_exact, tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_7_a_deferral_that_moves_the_retry_earlier_is_guarded.

E2a-8.statement:
**E2a-8 — Stop.** (D:42-43, D:123) A normal stop publishes `clean_stop` with the next due after final settlement,
best effort within a 2 s deadline (a collector that accepts and never answers does not delay the stop past it). A
writer-fault stop publishes nothing, so the wake state stays unknown. Tests:
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeServiceTests.test_E2a_8_a_normal_stop_publishes_clean_stop,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakePublisherTests.test_E2a_8_clean_stop_is_bounded_and_a_writer_fault_publishes_nothing,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_8_clean_stop_needs_settlement_and_a_final_due_read.
Review round 1: `clean_stop` is attempted only after verified final settlement (every thread stopped and settlement ran to its end) and a successful final read of the store's next due (its own read-only connection), and carries that value, never a cached one.
Decision 179: verified settlement means every run the exit pass knows of is released (not only that the pass ran); the writer fault is checked once more after the serve loop, so a stop signal never turns a writer-fault stop into a normal one. Tests: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_8_settlement_is_verified_only_when_every_run_is_released, tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_8_a_stop_signal_never_bypasses_the_writer_fault_check.

E2a-9.statement:
**E2a-9 — Reconcile marks unknown projects due; nothing starts.** (D:40-41) At collector start (before it reports
ready) and once per sweep interval (on a thread of its own, outside the sweep cycle's ledger hold), each active project with no wake row, a null or `pending` state, or a state other
than `clean_stop`, that no live host serves, is marked due now (`due_at_ms` = now); a `clean_stop` row keeps its
published due. The served check runs off the ledger lock; at most 64 projects per pass; a publication that lands
between the check and the mark is not overwritten. Nothing is started or spawned. Tests:
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeReconcileTests.test_E2a_9_unknown_projects_are_marked_due_at_collector_start_and_clean_stops_are_not,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeReconcileTests.test_E2a_9_a_newer_publication_is_not_overwritten_and_serving_projects_are_skipped,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_9_one_locked_read_examines_at_most_one_page_of_projects,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_9_reconcile_reaches_every_project_past_one_page,
tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeRoundOneTests.test_E2a_9_the_startup_pass_is_bounded_and_the_rest_follows.
Review round 1: a pass pages by rows examined (at most 64 project rows per locked read, by primary key, inactive and settled rows included), page after page from a saved cursor; a `clean_stop` row whose service left the unpublished-write marker counts unknown; the startup pass probes for at most 1 s and the wake thread finishes the rest at once.
Decision 179: each probe of a pass waits for a busy hint lock at most what is left of the pass's budget (`project_host_client.probe_deadline`), and a probe the budget cut short is not counted (the next pass probes that project again). Test: tests.test_e2a_wake_wire.WakeFinalFixTests.test_E2a_9_the_last_startup_probe_is_bounded_by_the_remaining_budget.

E2c-1.statement:
### E2c-1 - A stopped project with due holds starts by itself (E2-1, T1)
A registered project with a launch record, no live host and a due wake row (`project_wake.due_at_ms <= now`:
published by its last service, or marked due by E2a-9's reconcile because its state is unknown) is started by the
collector within one sweep interval (`STARTER_CHECK_SECONDS` apart), with no owner or client action. A project that
is not due is not started. **Acceptance (real collector and project host processes):** a project that never ran
(unknown: due at collector start) and one whose service published `clean_stop` with a past next due are both
serving within the interval, without any client command.

E2c-10.statement:
### E2c-10 - Stranded claims, timeouts and restarts (T11, T14; decision 150)
A claim carries its attempt id, claim time and, once spawned, the child's pid. At collector start (on the
starter's thread, before its first claim) and once per sweep interval, every outstanding claim that is not one of
this starter's own is reconciled: no child, or a child gone, releases it (a child gone without serving counts
failed); a surviving child keeps it until it serves or ends, and past twice the start timeout its own process group (the
child leads it: spawned with setsid) gets SIGKILL and the claim ends as failed only once that group is gone, so
never more than `START_SLOTS` started children live (decision 243). A spawned child is never left unowned
(decision 243): a pid record the ledger refuses is tried again for as long as the child lives; a clean stop before
it lands kills and reaps the child before its claim is released; a claim left without a pid is released only when
no process group led by that project's host exists. A claim never stays outstanding after a collector crash
longer than its child lives. The starter's own child still alive at twice `START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` gets SIGKILL to its
process group and counts failed. A service killed between its pending acknowledgement and its commit, or between
its commit and `exact`, is started within one interval; a collector restart keeps a project's failures and
backoff and reconciles unknown projects as due. **Acceptance:** a claim left by a dead collector with a dead child
is released and the project started; one with a live child is kept until that child ends; a host that never serves
is killed at twice the timeout; E2a's killed service is started; the backoff survives a collector restart.

E2c-11.statement:
### E2c-11 - Clean stop with the collector's intake closed (T13)
A project service stopping while the collector's account intake is closed (its socket gone or refusing) finishes
its best-effort `clean_stop` within the 2 s deadline and its stop is not delayed past it. **Acceptance:** a real
project host stopped after the collector is gone exits within the deadline plus its own stop.

E2c-2.statement:
### E2c-2 - Limits and lock discipline (E2-2, T2, T3)
Only the collector's starter thread starts projects. Its locked step only claims: one indexed read of due rows
(not parked, not backing off, no start outstanding; at most `START_CLAIM_BATCH`), each claimed row marked
outstanding with an attempt id and its claim time in the same transaction (`project_starts`), queued in memory
(at most `START_QUEUE_LIMIT`, a project at most once). Probing, verifying, hashing, spawning, waiting and reaping
run on the starter's own workers, off the ledger lock and never on the collector's request thread. At most one
start is outstanding per project and `START_SLOTS` overall; slots are refilled from the queue in claim order (due
order), so every due project is tried before any project is tried again (round robin). **Acceptance:** three due
projects, two of them ending at once: never more than 2 starts at once, never 2 for one project, the first three
starts name three different projects and retries alternate; while a start is blocked in its spawn, a collector
request that takes the ledger lock and a direct ledger read both complete, and the start then finishes.

E2c-3.statement:
### E2c-3 - Budgets (E2-2, T10; decision 150)
With 1,000 due projects the starter drains them (every one claimed and its attempt ended with an outcome) within
60 s; no claim step holds the ledger lock 750 ms or more and a 64-row claim batch takes under 50 ms; 1,000 due rows
add under 200 ms to collector start-up (nothing of the starter runs before ready); and the claim step's work does
not grow with 100,000 settled wake rows (rows with no due time). **Acceptance:** measured on a real ledger and a
real collector.

E2c-4.statement:
### E2c-4 - Backoff and the crash-loop park (E2-2, owner decision 143, T2)
A failed start (the host ended without serving, did not serve by twice `START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, or served but
ended within `START_PROBATION_SECONDS`) counts one failure of the project's streak; the first failure starts the
streak. The next attempt waits `START_BACKOFF_FIRST_SECONDS * 2^(failures-1)`, at most
`START_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS`. Failures and the streak are kept in the ledger (`project_starts`), so a collector
restart keeps them, and a publish never resets them. Once a start fails while the streak's first failure is
`START_PARK_AFTER_SECONDS` old, the project parks: `recovery failed: <reason_code>` and no further attempt. Only a
user action unparks: a new launch digest (setup ran again: a new install or update) or the owner's
`learning-start-project-service --project-root <root>` (owner-signed collector operation `start_unpark`, which also
ends the streak). A project reporting again (a publish) does not unpark it. A start that serves for
`START_PROBATION_SECONDS` ends the streak. **Acceptance:** a broken project backs off with growing waits; once
its streak is old enough it parks after its next failure; a republish leaves it parked; the owner command unparks;
a project that is fixed and serves ends its streak; a host killed within probation counts as failed. A probation
ends its streak only when its host is seen alive at or after the probation's end; a host found gone, however late
a restarted collector looks, counts failed (decision 243).

E2c-5.statement:
### E2c-5 - What is launched (E2-3, T6)
The child is the launch record's copy only: entry `<launch_copy>/.codex/orchestration/project_host.py`, run with
`PYTHON_ISOLATION_FLAGS`, environment exactly `{PATH: os.defpath, xcrun_nocache: "1"}`, its own session
(process group), stdin/stderr to /dev/null and stdout to a private report file. The copy is pinned
(`pin_runtime_copy`) from its verification until the child serves or ends. **Acceptance:** the running child's
arguments name the copy's entry and the isolation flags, and a variable planted in the collector's environment is
absent from the child's.

E2c-6.statement:
### E2c-6 - Install changed (E2-4, T4)
Before each start, off the lock, the copy's name must equal `launch_digest` and `launch_target_problem(copy, root,
{})` (the account's own home) must be None; otherwise nothing starts and the status is
`recovery pending: install changed`, checked again every `START_RECHECK_SECONDS` (no failure counted).
A project with no launch record is not started and keeps E2a-11's line. **Acceptance:** a changed copy file, a
changed project runtime file and a missing copy each give `recovery pending: install changed` and no spawn.

E2c-7.statement:
### E2c-7 - Another version's live service (E2-5, T5)
When a live host of another runtime serves the project, nothing starts, no maintenance is taken and the collector
does not stop; the status is `recovery: needs update handover: run learning-start-project-service --project-root
<root>`, checked again every `START_RECHECK_SECONDS`. **Acceptance:** with another runtime's live host, the line
and command shown, no spawn, the same collector process still serving and no maintenance marker.

E2c-8.statement:
### E2c-8 - Unattended pre-start steps (E2-8, T12)
Before spawning, the starter does the CLI's pre-start steps that need no collector maintenance: a project whose
learning is not moved and has no history is marked moved (the ledger's `mark_learning_moved_if_empty`); one with
history to migrate, or a pending activation, is not started (`recovery pending: learning migration: run
learning-start-project-service --project-root <root>`, checked again every `START_RECHECK_SECONDS`, no failure);
the collector never migrates, never takes maintenance and never stops itself for a start. A host that ends at once
keeps its fixed `SERVICE_START_REASONS` code from its private report file as the failure reason. A live compatible
host is never started again (E2b handles an unresponsive one). **Acceptance:** an empty project is marked moved and
then serves; a project with a pending activation is not started and shows the migration line; a host that ends at
once shows its own reason code in the status.

E2c-9.statement:
### E2c-9 - Status, scoped to its subject (E2-7 status part)
The owner-signed, read-only collector operation `start_status` (checked before any lookup, as E2a-11's
`launch_status`) answers `{"ok": true, "recovery": <line or null>}` for exactly the project its proof names, never
hold or result content: null when nothing is due or outstanding; `recovery: starting`; `recovery: started <UTC
time>`; `recovery: backing off (<n> failed: <reason_code>, next <UTC time>)`; `recovery failed: <reason_code>; stopped trying
after an hour of failed starts: run learning-start-project-service --project-root <root>`; `recovery pending:
install changed`; `recovery: needs update handover: <command>`; `recovery pending: learning migration:
<command>`; `recovery pending: service unresponsive` (a live compatible host whose due time is
`START_RECHECK_SECONDS` past). `learning-status` shows it as `recovery` when a launch record exists (E2a-11's line
otherwise). A request without the owner's proof gets the same refusal whether the root is registered or not; a
project session (no owner proof) sees null. attest has no status surface (unchanged). **Acceptance:** each line
over the real collector; unsigned requests for a registered and an unknown root get byte-identical refusals.

G1.statement: Every step exits 0, or refuses with a reason the step expects; a bare run_unavailable, account_unavailable or probe_unavailable is a failure.

G2.statement: Worker: every answer value matches the oracle; each required evidence outcome is pass or observed.

G3.statement: Verifier: opened for the worker's digest; each required evidence outcome is pass; no discrepancy; verdict pass or ready.

G5.statement: Capacity: after close, a supported per-run read shows every claimed run released, and the next billing probe gets a slot; final statistics show zero active or pending runs.

G6.statement: An update never needs the collector stopped by hand, also with a child running, and finishes with the collector healthy on the new build.

G7.statement: Records keep their history across every update: counts by kind, never content.

G8.statement: No private value (keys, fingerprints, paths under the temporary HOME) appears in any output that is saved, logged, reported or read by an AI helper (including the status command); a screen shown to the owner may show one only when the owner needs it to proceed or troubleshoot (owner decision 36).

G9.statement: A content-free JSON report with phases, seconds, reason codes and pass or fail per requirement is written, kept as the CI artifact.

H1c-1.statement: An account lane with unknown work is faulted, making restart due at the next check; status names held processes and the next action.

H1c-3.statement: The collector restarts only after every account lane child is proven gone; retained signature pipes close after proof.

HM2A-1.statement: A leftover prepare-* folder is removed only with positive proof that its owner is gone: its owner marker (written when the folder was made) names this state root and a launch-journal instance whose lock is free, and no live or pending record names it; no marker, another state root, a missing lock or a held lock (even after a clock jump) is never a removal. Removal is proven only by FileNotFoundError and reported fixed; a removal not proven is reported and retried. No mode is changed before that proof (a folder that is not listable is looked into through a search-only descriptor or not at all). A marker that could not be written in full (an open, write or close error) never fails the preparation and leaves no marker, so its folder is only reported.

HM2A-10.statement: register adds the check to a health monitor with the journal live set and the caller's pending reader; a pass removes an orphan and shows it.

HM2A-11.statement: The collector registers the workspaces check with a read-only pending reader over the project histories (no I/O at registration); a pass removes an orphan folder and keeps a live driver's folder.

HM2A-12.statement: A project whose history has no project_holds table (an older but valid store) owes no removals: it counts zero and does not fail the whole pending read; a corrupt or unreadable store still does.

HM2A-13.statement: Every remaining unknown pending read names its reason (too_many_projects, projects_unreadable:<Class>, history_unreadable:<Class>:<project id>, too_many_pending:<project id>, deadline); the workspaces finding carries it in its text and subject with a plain next step, within the existing length bounds. No dedupe exists in the health monitor for findings (it shows the last pass's findings), so none was added.

HM2A-2.statement: A folder a live driver owns (named by any launch-journal entry) or a young folder is kept.

HM2A-3.statement: A symlink, a foreign-owned folder or a file named like a preparation folder is reported and left exactly as it is, never followed.

HM2A-4.statement: A folder pending under decision 309 is left to the driver (no double removal); one still pending after PENDING_REPORT_PASSES passes is reported.

HM2A-5.statement: Path safety equals remove_recorded_workspace: absolute, no .., prepare-* name, the real scratch container as parent, a real folder owned by this user; an unsafe container removes nothing. Removal goes through pinned, fstat-verified directory descriptors, so swapping the container or a subfolder for a link mid-removal never reaches the link target. After owner proof a mode is changed only through fchmod on a descriptor opened O_NOFOLLOW and verified by fstat (device, inode, user), never by name, so a folder swapped in before the change keeps its mode.

HM2A-6.statement: Reads and work are bounded (entries examined and folders listed per pass with a rotating cursor so nothing is starved, removals and removed entries per pass, removal depth, the time share checked before every removal step, journal projects, names and entries, record items and paths); a folder not finished keeps its marker and resumes at the next pass (the last check comes before the marker goes, the folder's rmdir follows it at once, and a failed rmdir puts the marker back); every container entry read, however far the listing has gone, counts toward the scan cap and the time share is checked while listing, the listing going on across passes; each limit is in lifetime_caps.json with a past-the-limit test.

HM2A-7.statement: Records that cannot be read completely (an error or any truncation: listing, entry, item or distinct-path limits, counted while reading and after deduplication) mean nothing is removed and one finding says the records are incomplete; a check without both readers does nothing.

HM2A-8.statement: Findings are plain, closed, machine-scope, one sentence naming the folder and never a path, exception message or decision number.

HM2A-9.statement: The module never touches the ledger, history or preparation state: no SQLite or ledger import, its pending reader is injected (owner thread, E1b-1).

L1.1.statement: A fresh install through the scripted setup (S1 answers file and passphrase) finishes with every step ok, the protected command rule installed and the collector ready.

L1.2.statement: Setup run again on an installed project changes nothing: same files, same digests, no new records except its own checks; an answers-file re-run skips signing a billing statement that is already signed and current unless the answers ask to sign again (owner decision 37).

L10.1.statement: Hook events are recorded for a registered project's checkout and not for an unregistered project or from outside the checkout (the owner dropped the recording switch, PLAN-0.4.0.md decision at line 1363).

L10.2.statement: The learning history moves to the project store; learning-run-cycle runs.

L10.3.statement: Retention removes expired raw events and keeps their summaries (controllable clock).

L11.2.statement: A failed upgrade forced part-way leaves the records unchanged, the installer's automatic rollback of a failed update works and the next attempt succeeds.

L12.1.statement: From each earlier release tag (v0.3.1 on), with history built on it, an update to HEAD succeeds and the full run passes again.

L12.2.statement: A one-command update with an admitted-never-launched run and 0.2.x leftovers present needs no manual stop.

L12.3.statement: An update with a child really running goes ahead: the old child ends lost, status names the hand-over, finished results stay recordable, and nothing is half-installed at any step.

L12.4.statement: An update with uncommitted managed files is refused.

L12.5.statement: A second project updated after the first works (no other project stops working).

L12.6a.statement: History built on an earlier release with more than 512 admission records and a ledger over 128 MiB still opens, dispatches and upgrades (unbounded admission history).

L12.6b.statement: On that same long-history project, opening, dispatching and upgrading work with runs left by 0.2.x (including leftovers blocking updates) and a protected copy without role files; a busy billing probe reports its busy reason without masking it.

L12.7.statement: A dispatch refused at its claim on a project with long history closes by itself, and after an update from the release before, the next service closes any such run an earlier version left (0.3.3 C2, C3, C3f).

L13.1.statement: A session with danger-full-access, an unknown host, or opened above the project is refused with its reason.

L13.2.statement: The protected copy refuses a project it is not bound to.

L14.1.statement: learning-status, learning-run-status, earlier_version_runs and learning-orchestration-report give the right values at each phase, and none is private.

L15.1.statement: learning-delete-project removes the project's records and services and leaves another project untouched.

L16.1.statement: Hook events from two projects and account calls arriving at once, through the installed product, are each written or answered exactly once: every event is in the ledger once (its own project, counted again by the collector's status), every account request id is recorded once however often it is sent, and the owner queue refuses nothing inside its limits (E2: hooks and account calls at once; no lost or duplicated request).

L16.2.statement: While a large project's hook backlog drains, a small project's events are written among them, not after them: no project is starved (E2: fair turns; the one-turn-per-round order itself is proved by the in-process owner load test, because real processes never queue deeply enough to show it).

P9-1.statement:
### P9-1 — Claims use current verified applicable evidence

After collector maintenance, a public deferred claim succeeds with an attestation capture limit of two despite three valid attestations for the same account/provider whose superseded rows remain cited. The latest verified applicable attestation wins, with source sequence breaking observation-time ties. Another account and another provider cannot replace it, and an invalid newer stored signature cannot supersede it. Admission and standalone signature capture use the same attestation candidates. The deferred job's aggregate admission budget remains separate from its two-attestation regression boundary.

P9-2.statement:
### P9-2 — Collector maintenance preserves references and makes bounded progress

The collector's own sweep cycle uses independent inspection and deletion rowid cursors. Each pass examines at most a batch of deletion candidates even when they are cited, removes eligible uncited superseded attestations in bounded batches, retains cited records and signatures, and eventually finishes across repeated cycles. References remain readable through the repository. A signature row alone never proves supersession; only a verified later attestation for the same project, account and provider permits deletion.

P9-3.statement:
### P9-3 — Projection is derived and fails closed on changes

Supersession results are connection-local derived data, never durable signature authority. Results bind exact stored content, digest, source, sequence, observation time, signature and owner generation. A changed input or owner generation invalidates its cached result; uncached inputs remain candidates until checked. Capture performs no cryptography or writes, and the worker still verifies captured signatures and exact recapture before admission. Restart requires collector maintenance to rebuild the projection. Verification runs outside the ledger lock and account transaction, then records a verdict only after exact row and owner-generation recheck. Both valid and invalid verdicts are cached for unchanged inputs and generation. Verifier exceptions (including subprocess timeouts) leave rows unchecked for retry. No persistent schema or record shape changes.

P9-4.statement:
### P9-4 — Remaining capture candidates retain hard quotas

After maintenance, exact checked foreign-provider rows are excluded from signature capture. Unknown or changed rows are conservatively charged before provider filtering. Row and byte quotas still refuse overflow before copying bodies, and malformed metadata still refuses safely. Cited superseded history is retained independently of these capture quotas.

The P9-4 header, body and admission selection queries use indexed materialized candidate membership before ordering and limiting. SQLite VM work for a claim with zero versus 10,000 retained cited superseded rows differs by only a small constant. Unchecked rows remain charged.

Work-budget and deadline refusal tests exercise unchecked candidate history, which is still charged, while unrelated events can be skipped by the candidate index. Refusal still precedes body copying and restores the read scope and owner connection.

P9b-1.statement:
### P9b-1 — Only definitive verifier results are cached

An unsafe verifier executable or parent (symlink, wrong owner, writable mode),
or an unavailable, killed, out-of-memory or otherwise failed verifier, must
raise in the maintenance authority's `raise_verifier_failures` mode. Its row
stays unchecked, charged and retryable without restart. Only a clean successful
verification or clean definitive ssh-keygen signature-invalid result can be
cached. Existing non-maintenance callers continue to fail closed.

Final targeted fix on `1e6b5e13` (confirming review `040-p9b-r2c`): a
nonzero verifier result is definitive invalid only for exit 255 with stdout
exactly `Could not verify signature.` (optionally terminated by LF or CRLF),
and stderr either empty or containing only exact allowlisted diagnostic lines.
The allowlist is the following eight lines observed from real OpenSSH 10.5p1
malformed/truncated, payload-mismatch or wrong-namespace signatures (LF and CRLF are accepted):

- `Couldn't parse signature: missing footer`
- `Couldn't parse signature: missing header`
- `sig_verify: sshsig_armor: invalid format`
- `sshsig_dearmor: decode base64: invalid format`
- `Couldn't verify signature: invalid format`
- `sshsig_peek_hashalg: parse signature object: incomplete message`
- `Couldn't verify signature: namespace does not match`
- `Signature verification failed: incorrect signature`

Any other stderr line, including an extra unknown line after a known diagnostic,
is non-definitive. Infrastructure diagnostics always take precedence, including
`memory allocation failed`, `libcrypto error: x`, `error in libcrypto`,
`Unable to open allowed keys file F: Too many open files`,
`Unable to open allowed keys file F: Input/output error`, and
`Couldn't read signature file: Input/output error`; arbitrary strerror text is
never allowlisted. Unsafe prechecks, timeouts, signals, other exit codes,
missing/extra stdout and all other ambiguous results remain non-definitive.
Their rows stay unchecked, capturable and retryable without restart. Existing
infrastructure-precedence assertions remain in place.

Real ssh-keygen regressions must prove wrong-key, truncated and wrong-namespace
signatures are cached invalid without verification on the next maintenance
pass. With this OpenSSH version an empty allowed-signers file or a directory
used as allowed-signers can produce exit 255, exact rejection stdout and empty
stderr, just like a wrong key: those outputs are deliberately definitive invalid
under this contract. A reported allowed-signers or signature-file I/O diagnostic
is non-definitive regardless of its strerror. Existing constructor checks still
reject a directory already present at authority creation; the output contract
also covers a path changed after that check. No new signer-path precheck is
part of this fix.

P9b-2.statement:
### P9b-2 — Candidate membership contains only attestations

`temp.capture_candidates` contains billing attestations only. Insert, update,
restart and projection rebuild preserve that restriction. Candidate count and
the per-open candidate rebuild's SQLite VM work are independent of unrelated
non-attestation history. Admission still captures all relevant evidence families
under its existing time, project, source and quota rules, excluding unrelated
history. Both public capture boundaries retain bounded superseded-history work.

Review fix round: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN must show indexed admission-union access
without a full records scan. Each union branch supplies at most the capture
limit (including its overflow sentinel) before the final rowid sort and
record/signature joins. This preserves the exact globally ordered prefix and
overflow refusal while bounding the rows materialized for that final sort;
the existing SQL work/deadline budget still governs scope filtering.

P9b-3.statement:
### P9b-3 — Record deletion restores surviving predecessors

Deleting a billing attestation by any record-deletion path rebuilds the derived
supersession state for its project/account/provider. Deleting the newest valid
row immediately restores the latest surviving verified predecessor as a capture
candidate, without restart or re-verification. Other accounts and providers
remain independent. Deleting superseded rows must preserve bounded sweep work.

PREPCLEAN-1.statement: Twelve failed physical preparation-folder removals retain the folder, slot, byte reservations and live memory holds; attempt thirteen observes actual removal before retirement. A missing child exception is not workspace removal proof.

PREPCLEAN-2.statement: Preparation cleanup retries continue indefinitely with monotone one-to-sixty-second capped backoff, no early requests and bounded retry state. Pending cleanup retains its live custodian across the automatic idle replacement boundary; replacement resumes after observed removal.

PREPCLEAN-3.statement: Status and the terminal warning list plainly say a preparation folder could not be removed, background retries continue and its slot remains held. Clear the warning after removal and expose no private path or exception text. The summary never promises automatic replacement while a removal is pending; a pending folder whose location the service never learned says so and says what can be done.

PREPCLEAN-4.statement: A pending folder removal never blocks service replacement or an update: it is recorded durably in the preparation hold row (folder path, removal pending) and survives the stop, release or crash of the service that owned it. The successor loads the records, keeps retrying with the same capped backoff and keeps the warning until the folder is observed absent, then records the removal as proven. Only this host's own preparation folders are ever removed.

RECOV-1.statement:
**RECOV-1 — A healthy serving service does not report unresponsive while evidence is pending.**
After the initial validated history open, and after a periodic maintenance pass on the project history writer
whose maintenance steps all succeeded, publish an exact next check no earlier
than that pass's wall time when a hold deadline remains overdue. Repeat this for every successful pass, even if no
hold changed. Keep future deadlines and null (no outstanding deadline) unchanged. In particular, an expired
releasing reservation may legitimately wait for verified account closure while an account binding remains held
until a future `next_eligible`; neither that wait nor evidence-only holds imply an unresponsive project service.
Acceptance: the real writer pass, publisher, ledger start record and recovery formatter keep returning null across
more than START_RECHECK_SECONDS of successful passes with an unchanged overdue releasing reservation; a future
deadline is preserved. Subsequent hold transactions retain the last completed check as a floor for live exact
publications, without renewing it, including a real hold write committed through the history store between passes.
No hold is released or rescheduled by this status correction.

RECOV-2.statement:
**RECOV-2 — The published orchestration check respects B6 backoff.**
The wake query uses max(due_at_ms, next_check_ms) for each held orchestration, then takes the earliest check across
all outstanding holds and withdrawal retries. A B6 refusal must invalidate the queued publication before changing
its next check, and publish the updated exact check after commit. Released tombstones do not contribute.
Acceptance: the real unattended close backs off a blocked orchestration and publishes its future retry; another
earlier due hold still wins; releasing its execution obligation resets the orchestration check through the existing
B6 release path. Before resetting a held orchestration's retry to its earlier due time, publish `pending` under
E2a-7, so a crash before the next exact publication cannot leave the collector holding the later retry.

RECOV-3.statement:
**RECOV-3 — Preserve E2c-9's stuck-service signal and stopped-service recovery.**
After the initial validated history open, only a periodic history-writer maintenance pass whose maintenance steps
all succeeded supplies progress. A suppressed failure in any maintenance step prevents renewal for that pass,
while the remaining cleanup steps still run. Status reads, a serving process,
the publisher's sender thread, unrelated writes and failed maintenance do not renew this check. If progress stops
and a serving project's published due time is at least START_RECHECK_SECONDS past, keep the exact line
`recovery pending: service unresponsive`, including at the threshold. A clean stop publishes the actual outstanding
deadline, including an overdue evidence obligation, so the collector still wakes a stopped project conservatively.
Acceptance: no completed pass and a failed pass leave the overdue warning; after successful passes stop, the warning
returns at the threshold, including when one sub-step fails persistently inside otherwise completed passes;
clean_stop retains the raw overdue deadline. Existing E2c-9 assertions stay unchanged.

RS-10-DUE.statement: 1,000 due holds drain, at the start pass's own batch size of 64 (direct calls, scheduling excluded), within ceil((1000+64)/64)+1 = 18 batches, at most 64 released per batch, each batch under 50 ms (median of three repeats) and in total under 60 s. The production path is RS-10-DUE-PROD.
