RS-10-FLAT.statement: The start pass's work is flat as released history grows (small scale in the suite; 100,000 released leases and reservations in scripts/measure_s13.py).

RS-B-4.statement: Instance-bound driver and preparation rows commit before their effects, retire only after memory retirement, and recover only from positive stopped-instance evidence; preserve withdrawal and handoff custody (M1-M8, I1, L4, L6, L7).

RS-B-5.statement:
**RS-B-5 — Authenticated withdrawal of an unclaimed open.**
The project service and the opening host class may withdraw an unclaimed open with matching enrolled project,
caller scope, run id, inputs digest, attempt custody and current binding generation. Authentication precedes
immutable receipt replay; an exact replay remains available after the binding is pruned. Different callers receive
no receipt. New transitions refuse claimed, fenced, withdrawn or stale bindings; missing generations are refused.
Withdrawal evidence is retained for the tombstone's life. The project records its withdrawal duty before registration,
marks the complete request releasing before dropping memory, retries identical requests after lost replies, and
withdraws never-claimed cancellations, pre-preparation failures, idle registrations (one hour, owner decision 90.7)
and stopped-service registrations. A registration refusal preserves the duty; a faulted writer gets one memory
withdrawal, otherwise account expiry. Armed leases belong to the fence path.
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-B.md draft 3 §4, §7 and rows W1-W5 (W4a-e), M7; PLAN-0.4.0-supervisor-slices.md B3.

RS-B-9-B1.statement: Per normal run, the added writer work of all RS-B register transactions (reserve, arm, bind, commit, reservation release, including the reservation/hold JOIN inside _release_obligation) plus the commit cost the register rows add plus the memory-hold transactions is under 5 ms in total, measured on the real operations (one warm-up run, then the median of five).

RS-B-9-B6.statement: One eligible unarmed lease behind 128 blocked (live) leases, with 50 new blocked arrivals before every batch, is released within 4 start-pass batches, at most 64 released per batch, the median wall-clock of each batch position under 50 ms over repeated runs; the pass does equal SQLite work with and without released lease history. This is the observable budget; the section 5 mechanism is RS-B-9-B6-MECH.

RS-B-9-B6-MECH.statement: RS-B draft 4 section 5 (bounded selection, back-off, re-due order): a start-pass batch selects at most 64 rows and a blocked row gets a back-off so later batches do not examine it before it is due.

RS-B-B4.statement:
**RS-B-B4 — Lost-run settlement reaches the project store.**
A run whose service was lost after its claim was admitted is settled at the account (`account.settle_lost_run`, reply
shape unchanged) and its settlement then reaches the project store as a closure the project writer verifies with its own
result key: a NEW account operation, `account.lost_run_closure`, answers a settled (`lost`) or released
(`released_unacknowledged`) run with a closure bound to the project, run handle, attempt, lease digest, assignment digest,
bridge run id (the claim id), release kind, the account's release time and the outbox request's digest (RS-B-B4-1).
Before any account call the attempt's register row (its reservation hold, or its lease hold when the claim was never bound)
is `releasing` with the request id and request digest; after any crash the identical request is re-sent until the closure
is stored, and a closure naming another request digest is refused with nothing written; account calls stay one at a time
on the driver's helper thread (RS-B-B4-2). `record_account_settlement(lease_binding, closure)` verifies the closure and, in
one writer transaction, inserts the settlement row, expires a `claim_pending` lease and releases its hold `lost_unbound`,
moves a `reserved` reservation to `retiring` (a committed body is left to retention), releases the reservation hold with
the closure's kind and receipt, and releases unfinished custody `lost_with_reservation`; it writes nothing to the terminal
outbox, execution consumptions, cleanup receipts or admission records, and its two register writes are the ones D2/D4
planted (RS-B-B4-3). At every driver caller the order is: account reply, settlement committed, workspace removed, journal
`settled`; a stop between steps leaves the journal entry unsettled and the next sweep replays the identical request
(RS-B-B4-4). A reservation with a verified settlement row is finished for `_unfinished` (checked before the consumption
check) and released for the purge (`_attempt_released`); no reader counts it as a successful run (RS-B-B4-5). An
identical retry after settlement returns the stored receipt, also from the register tombstone after the purge; another
project, lease digest, claim id or attempt is refused with every table unchanged; a purged identity can never be taken
again (RS-B-B4-6). The register validator refuses a settlement row whose hold is not released with the same kind, and a
held reservation with a settlement row; `releasing` without one is legal (RS-B-B4-7). With every bound set to 2, three
runs lost after their claim are settled, their orchestrations close, their rows purge, and a fourth run dispatches,
records and closes (RS-B-B4-8). RC-3 runs un-skipped (RS-B-B4-9).
Prerequisite (§9): the account's digest key and the project writer's result key are the same file
(`<state root>/digest.key`) in every install path, and a run can only be claimed after the account verified the
project's sealed lease with its key, so every closure is verifiable at the project.
Source: ANALYSIS-0.4.0-rsb-b4-b7.md §0, §2, §9; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-B.md draft 2 §4, draft 3 §6, §14; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md SH-3, SH-5, SH-7; docs/requirements/b4s.md.

RS-B-B4m-1.statement:
**RS-B-B4m-1 — One local update command.** One function builds the exact terminal command
from the local install record: change into the installing clone, then run `./setup.sh <project>`
and choose Configure. All three compatibility refusal sites use it, name the version holding
the state, and use plain words. Collector replies never supply command paths or executable text.

RS-B-B4m-2.statement:
**RS-B-B4m-2 — Preserve existing reply fields.** A newer collector/account never adds or removes
fields of an existing account/history operation's reply. New data requires a new operation.
The guard compares every existing operation with the previous-release field catalogue, retaining
the optional field variants already allowed by that release.

RS-B-B4m-3.statement:
**RS-B-B4m-3 — Help already-installed clients.** Troubleshooting and release notes name
`status_collector_unavailable` and `runtime_newer`, show the clone/project terminal command,
and direct already-installed 0.3.x users to Configure.

RS-B-B4t-0.statement: Update with a child running proceeds; lost settlement, retained committed custody and phase recovery; all other preflight refusals write nothing.

RS-B-B4t-1.statement: No idle wait or manual stop for a verified predecessor.

RS-B-B4t-10.statement: Every named phase resumes with one effect, including internal migration and atomic-file crash cuts.

RS-B-B4t-2.statement: Committed results and open/paused orchestrations stay recordable under current authority.

RS-B-B4t-3.statement: Proven predecessor exit before adoption; lifetime lock and epoch fence; schema and version floor prevent reopen.

RS-B-B4t-4.statement: Updated project's running children end lost; other work follows D2.5 and other projects survive.

RS-B-B4t-5.statement: One recording or settlement effect per binding across versions and retries.

RS-B-B4t-6.statement: Primary recheck remains idempotent across takeover.

RS-B-B4t-7.statement: Existing B4m commands and documented installed-old-client refusals remain accurate.

RS-B-B4t-8.statement: Status names each takeover outcome using D2.8 wording without changing existing reply shapes.

RS-B-B4t-9.statement: Unknown lineage or corrupt custody is refused and held, never guessed or freed.

RS-B-B5a.statement:
**RS-B-B5a — Crashed settlement in process mode.** Acceptance items RS-B-B5a-1 to RS-B-B5a-6 follow; the tests cite the group id.

- **RS-B-B5a-1 — Positive, recorded process evidence.** A process journal entry
  may advance from `watched` to durable `gone` only after `tree_state` returns
  `gone`: child and watchdog identities (PID plus kernel birth) have exited,
  the watchdog recorded its whole-tree cleanup confirmation, and two kernel
  checks find no group/session members or processes carrying the run marker.
  A live child/descendant, missing confirmation, unreadable/ambiguous evidence,
  `spawning`, `launched`, or a container entry proves nothing. Age never proves
  a project-side crash. `gone` retains the identities and cannot launch again.
- **RS-B-B5a-2 — Account closure.** Reuse `account.lost_run_closure`, with exactly
  its existing reply fields and request. A slot whose recorded account release
  is `crashed` receives a closure of kind `crashed` only with this run's durable
  process `gone` (or already `settled`) journal entry. Match the complete lease,
  run, attempt, claim request and bridge ID. The admitted-unbound exception is
  a durable never-spawned admission (`claimed`, or its `settled` tombstone,
  with no child, watchdog or run marker). Until then the existing
  `claim_cleanup_unavailable` refusal remains, including B4s's live-child test.
  RS-A's existing timed account-slot rule is unchanged; it cannot authorize
  release of a project reservation. No new account operation or op-set pin.
- **RS-B-B5a-3 — Writer evidence gate, V3/V7.** A signed `crashed` closure alone
  cannot release a reservation. Before the first settlement the writer reads
  the matching protected process journal entry and requires recorded `gone` or
  `settled` evidence with child/watchdog identities. Missing, mismatched,
  unreadable, container or pruned-first evidence refuses with every table
  unchanged. Its proof is saved in the released hold's `evidence` in the same
  transaction as the B4s closure and register release. A claim_pending lease
  with the matching never-spawned admission is marked `admitted_unbound` by the
  outbox writer; only that lease can use the exception, never a bound reservation.
  A fence's authenticated `claimed` answer is journaled before arbitration and
  keeps the stopped intent's instance so a failed settlement retries next sweep.
- **RS-B-B5a-4 — Exactly once, shared outbox.** Preserve B4s arbitration and
  request digest fencing; replay the identical request after a stop. Record
  `crashed` once through `record_account_settlement`, then remove the workspace,
  then mark the journal `settled`. An identical retry, including after journal
  pruning or attempt purge, returns the stored receipt with `known: true`.
  Another key/project/run/attempt/lease/claim/request is refused without writes.
- **RS-B-B5a-5 — Custody and readers, X4.** An uncommitted crashed reservation
  retires and releases unfinished custody `lost_with_reservation`; a committed
  result and its custody remain for retention. No terminal, consumption,
  cleanup receipt or outcome is invented. The existing verified-settlement
  readers allow close/purge and never count the run as successful. Existing
  never-spawned admitted claims release their lease through B4s `lost_unbound`,
  including an account slot already marked `crashed`; they are not described
  as an exited child (A5/L6b).
- **RS-B-B5a-6 — Plain status and compatibility.** A lost run with capacity
  still held explains that process-exit confirmation/settlement is pending;
  a released one says its capacity was released, with unknown outcome. Preserve
  status fields and all existing account/history reply field sets. Keep every
  existing assertion unchanged; if any needs changing, stop and record exact
  old → new in `b5a/assertions.md`.

Implementation and test map, red evidence and commands are in
[b5a/validation.md](b5a/validation.md).

RS-B-B6-1.statement:
**RS-B-B6-1 — Every orchestration has a register row.**
> Every orchestration has a register row: taken when created, released `closed` by the primary's close or
> `end_earlier`, `interrupted_unattended` by the unattended close, each in the close's own transaction. Existing open
> orchestrations are adopted in a 20 -> 21 step only; the validator then refuses an open orchestration without a held row.

Acceptance: `orchestration.open` writes, in its own transaction, a held `orchestration` row (identity = handle,
`taken_at_ms` = open time, `due_at_ms` = open time + ORCHESTRATION_IDLE_MS). Every later non-close mutation
(checkpoint, pause, resume) moves `due_at_ms` to its own time + ORCHESTRATION_IDLE_MS. The primary's close releases it
`closed` (evidence `{"by":"primary"}`), `end_earlier` releases it `closed` (evidence `ended_by_update_unrecorded`, as
RS-D N1), the unattended close releases it `interrupted_unattended` (evidence `{"by":"unattended"}`). A failure writing
the release rolls the close back (the orchestration stays open, its row held). The register validator (SH-7, run at
open, at restore and inside the step) refuses: an open orchestration without a held row; a held row whose orchestration
is closed or missing. An ordinary open never adopts.

RS-B-B6-2.statement:
**RS-B-B6-2 — Eligibility of the unattended close, inside its transaction.**
> No held lease or reservation of that orchestration, `_unfinished` false, effective now (`max(wall, floor)`) >=
> `due_at_ms` (24 h after last activity). Memory kinds are not checked: a live registered run with no lease is refused
> new work by the existing `active_for` gates after the close.

Acceptance: inside the close's transaction the unattended close refuses (`history_orchestration_pending`, nothing
written) when any reservation of the orchestration has a held or releasing register row, when `_unfinished` is true
(covers held leases: a held lease row is exactly a live lease, SH-7), or when effective now < `due_at_ms`. Effective now
is `max(wall, persisted floor)` read without moving the floor: a wall clock moved back below the floor still closes at
the floor. Taking an execution hold (lease or reservation) of the orchestration is activity: `due_at_ms` moves to at
least its time + ORCHESTRATION_IDLE_MS, in the take's own transaction (releasing one is not activity, B6-4). After the
close, `active_for` refuses new work for that orchestration
(`history_orchestration_state`).

RS-B-B6-3.statement:
**RS-B-B6-3 — A crash-replay of the unattended close is the identical request.**
Acceptance: the unattended close's request id is derived from (orchestration handle, expected sequence) with the
store's key (`end-idle-<32 hex>`), never random. Applying the same derived request again answers `known: true` with the
same receipt and writes nothing; two passes or two stores built from the same state derive the same id.

RS-B-B6-4.statement:
**RS-B-B6-4 — Fairness: next check, back-off, reset.**
Acceptance: one pass selects held orchestration rows by `next_check_ms` (ascending, at most UNATTENDED_CLOSE_BATCH = 4
per pass; the service passes 4), only rows with `next_check_ms <= now` and `due_at_ms <= now`, through a partial index
(`project_holds_orchestration_check`). A row that is due but refused (B6-2) backs off: its first refusal sets
`next_check_ms = now + 10 s`, each later one doubles the wait, capped at 5 min. Releasing any execution hold (lease or
reservation) of that orchestration resets its `next_check_ms` to 0 (and the back-off) in the release's own transaction.
A blocked row never stops a later due row from closing in the same pass.

RS-B-B6-5.statement:
**RS-B-B6-5 — Cleanup rows of closed orchestrations (K1, K2).**
Acceptance K1: a never-admitted attempt (lease released `withdrawn_unsent`, no reservation) of a closed orchestration,
past its reserved time + RESULT_PURGE_GRACE_MS, has its lease and cleanup rows purged by the expiry pass, through its
register release: the lease row's released tombstone stays, and the orchestration's row stays released.
K2: an admitted attempt (reservation exists, committed and recorded) of a closed orchestration with no account release
acknowledgement and no settlement is never purged, however late: its reservation, lease and cleanup rows stay and its
reservation register row stays held.

RS-B-B6-6.statement:
**RS-B-B6-6 — Changed runtime (RS-D N1, N2).**
Built by RS-D S2 (`docs/requirements/rsd-runtime-close.md`); re-run green here on the new step: eligible -> closed and
custody `orchestration_closed`, unrecorded ones counted; unfinished stays open with custody kept.

RS-B-B6-7.statement:
**RS-B-B6-7 — Schema step 20 -> 21 (decision 131).**
Acceptance: the store format is 21. The step is additive: it adds `project_orchestrations.state`
(`TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'`, `open` or `closed`), the index `project_orchestrations_state(project_id,state)`, the
partial index `result_reservations_live(project_id) WHERE state<>'expired'` (RS-D S3) and the partial index
`project_holds_orchestration_check(project_id,next_check_ms) WHERE kind='orchestration' AND state='held'` (B6-4). It
runs only on the authorized upgrade path (an ordinary open of a 20 store is refused, `history_incompatible`, the file
unchanged), as ONE transaction with the existing step machinery: copy kept first (`history.sqlite3.before-21.*`, same
backup format), every DDL, the state backfill, the adoption (each open orchestration without a row gets a held row,
evidence `{"adopted":21}`, `due_at_ms` = last activity + 24 h; closed ones and existing tombstones are left as they are)
and both validators before commit. Any failure (process death included) leaves the store at 20, its rows unchanged
and the copy removed; a later attempt upgrades. A repeated open of the 21 store changes nothing. A 20 store with an
unknown object (trigger, table, index) is refused before any write. Records-upgrade: a real store written by the
step-20 runtime (0.8.57, `tests/fixtures/history_step20/store.sql`, generated by `make_store.py` with that runtime)
upgrades with every pre-existing row byte-identical (orchestrations gain only `state`), its orchestrations' states
match their checkpoints, the active and paused ones are adopted held, and the closed ones still close-, purge- and
report- as before.

RS-B-B6-8.statement:
**RS-B-B6-8 — Indexed orchestration state (decisions 185, 187).**
Acceptance: every open/close writes `state` in the same statement as the checkpoint pointer. Counting open
orchestrations (`_open_count`, the open limit) reads only `project_orchestrations_state`, never a checkpoint blob
(work equal at 0 and 1,000 closed orchestrations, measured as SQLite VM steps). Integration note: batch 3's
`OrchestrationCountsCostTests` (not on this base) is to be un-skipped against this column when batches merge.

RS-B-B7-4.statement:
`history.holds_report` adds `recovery_pending` with exactly `reasons` and `stale`.
`reasons` always contains five keys with nonnegative counts when fresh and null
counts when stale: `needs_settlement`,
`needs_process_evidence`, `has_holds`, `stop_failed`, `account_unreachable`.
Each unresolved row has one current reason (RS-B draft 3 §10). Reservation holds
and closing_denied/admitted_unbound leases default to `needs_settlement`, even
without a readable journal entry. More specific observations replace that reason:
`needs_process_evidence` when disappearance is unproved, `stop_failed` after a
failed container stop, and `account_unreachable` after an actual transport failure.
A later successful observation clears the failure. `has_holds` counts open
orchestrations blocked by live execution holds. Current failed admitted runs are
included; ordinary active runs do not acquire a failure observation.
The driver publishes an immutable project-local observation after a complete sweep;
the owner also publishes its failed-run/backoff observations without refreshing
the sweep age; run identities deduplicate overlapping observations internally. The
writer adds its current has_holds count without reading journal files or result
contents. No observation means stale. A reading is stale strictly after twice
EXPIRY_SECONDS since its last completed observation, using monotonic time. Failed
or incomplete sweeps do not refresh it. A restart begins stale. No identities,
paths, digests, result bodies, exception text or other project data are returned.

Tests: `tests.test_b7b_recovery` (real store and driver sweep with controlled external
boundaries); `tests.test_b7b_terminal` (plain isolated Python terminal, real framed
history exchange where sockets are permitted).

RS-B-B7-5.statement:
Measure the combined code, report raw numbers and failures without loosening limits:
B1 added register writer work of a normal run <5 ms; B2 1,000 held rows startup
overhead <=100 ms; B3 a 64-row batch <50 ms; B4 equal query work at 0/100,000
tombstones and partial index plans; B5 1,000 eligible rows behind 64 blocked rows
within ceil((1000+64)/64)+1 = 18 batches, and one eligible behind 128 blocked rows
within 4; B6 the latter with re-due blocked rows and 50 arrivals/batch still within
4. RS-D S3: retirement of 10 <50 ms, outcome lookup <5 ms, startup overhead with
64 live contexts <=200 ms; compare retirement/lookup/reconciliation work at
0/100,000 tombstones. Measure product operations, not a substitute scheduler.
Missing operations or unavailable service startup measurements are reported as
unmeasured/failed, never inferred from design or a cheaper proxy.
Measured B3, B4, B5 and S3 retirement/lookup limits are executable assertions.
B4 includes 100,000 released lease and reservation rows as well as custody/context
tombstones, and measures recovery_pending including its has_holds query. Attempt
identities split at their single colon: the run-handle grammar excludes colons,
and the identity constructor must raise ValueError for a colon, including under -O.
Missing memory hold tracking stays asserted while B1/B6 remain unmeasured.
Probe Unix socket binding with try/except OSError. When available, measure actual
ProjectServiceHost startup (writer bootstrap, RunDriver, listeners and published runtime hint)
with 1,064 held leases versus empty (B2 <=+100 ms) and 64 live contexts versus none
(S3 <=+200 ms), assert both limits and mark service_startup_status met only when met.
When binding is unavailable, retain store-open proxies, record unmeasured plus the
OSError reason, and skip only the service-startup subtest; never require bind failure.
Timing bounds use one warm-up then the median of three runs of the real operation;
destructive operations receive equivalent fresh work for every run. VM-step equality
at 0/100,000 tombstones remains the primary invariant.

Tests/harness: `tests.test_b7b_budgets`; measured results and exact scope will be
recorded below and in `b7b/STATUS.md`.

RS-B-B7-6.statement:
Grow report and closed response validator together; require every new key, reject
extra keys, bool/negative counts and non-bool stale. Capacity report stays unchanged.
`learning-status` prints recovery_pending (null if unavailable), through the existing
project enrollment and authorization. The plain-terminal test checks the real
new response shape, foreign project rejection, and output privacy. Existing B7a
exact-top-level assertion must grow with the report; record the replacement in
`b7b/assertions.md`. No other existing assertions may be weakened.
When recovery is stale, learning-status also prints the plain sentence
"Recovery was not checked recently." and all five reported counts are null.
The response validator accepts null counts only when stale; fresh null counts,
negative/bool counts, missing/extra keys and non-bool stale remain invalid.
A history-only service (ProjectServiceHost with bundle_root=None) serves the
report without a RunDriver and must therefore return stale until a completed
observation exists. A client with an older runtime digest is refused with
history_not_authorized before authorization or report computation; the gate is
the service's runtime-digest equality check, not an assumed old-client decoder.

Sweep-local account failure capture is reset in a finally, including when
post-sweep cleanup/publication raises. A refusal (account_not_authorized or
account_wrong_owner) beside a transport failure must count only the latter as
account_unreachable.

RS-D-2-N1.statement:
**RS-D-2-N1 — Changed-runtime custody after B4t.**
Accepted B4t Draft 2 D2.11 supersedes the interim runtime-only close. A runtime
change does not close an open or paused orchestration or release its committed
custody. Verified predecessor custody stays recordable under current authority;
unknown or newer custody stays held. Ordinary primary close, rollover, idle and
retention rules still apply. Existing legacy `ended_by_update_unrecorded` counts
remain readable without adding a new update-only close or changing reply fields.

RS-D-2-N2.statement:
**RS-D-2-N2 — Unfinished changed-runtime custody.**
Without verified account release, an unrecorded result prevents close. Keep the orchestration
open and committed body/context custody charged until its retention deadline; at that deadline
release custody `retention`, without inventing release evidence or counting an update closure.
Corrupt release evidence cannot close it. No pre-commit deadline retires reserved custody (SH-4).

RS-D-9-S2.statement:
**RS-D-9-S2 — History-independent selection work.**
On equivalent live data, the retirement selector, stored worker context lookup by
outcome, and context sweep visit equal rows with zero and 100,000 retired
tombstones. Count SQLite work, not elapsed time.

RS-D-9-S3.statement:
**RS-D-9-S3 — Partial query indexes.**
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for those production statements uses the relevant partial
indexes and never scans the tombstone table. Check both the first page and the
cursor page of the two fair selectors.

RS-D-D2.statement:
**RS-D-D2 — Deadlines and retention of result custody.**
No deadline before the commit retires a lease-born reservation: a reserved row past its lease deadline stays charged and
publishable while its RS-B obligation is held, and is retired only after RS-B releases that obligation (SH-4, RS-4);
a row that lacks its hold is kept and reported, never retired by a deadline. Committed custody is released `retention`
exactly at `retained_until_ms`, judged at max(wall, persisted floor), so a moved-back clock revives nothing and blocks no
pass (RS-D-7). A closed orchestration releases committed custody `orchestration_closed`, but an unattended close does not
end custody (owner decision 90.8). A verifier opens only when its worker outlasts the verifier's lease by one hour (owner
decision 90.4); a worker expiring while the verifier runs leaves the verifier's custody live, and a record on an expired
attempt is refused. A retiring row refuses body, context and admission reads. Only the lease path (`prepare_lease`) is
reachable from product code: the non-lease `prepare` is refused at runtime on any lane built without the local-reference allowance (the service runtime's lane).
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-D.md draft 2 s1, s8, s9, draft 3 s8, rows D1-D4, C1-C3, V1-V4; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md SH-3, SH-4; docs/requirements/d2.md.

RS-D-D3.statement:
**RS-D-D3 — Crash-safe retirement and the context sweep.**
Retirement records `retiring` (custody released, reads refused), unlinks the fixed names without opening or following them
(a missing, corrupt, wrong-mode, extra-hard-link, symlink, FIFO or link-pair entry is unlinked as an entry), fsyncs the
directory, and only then records `expired`; a stop at any step is finished by the next pass, and the charge is kept until
`expired`. Only a directory under a fixed name needs repair: the row stays `retiring` and charged, its context is
`repair_required` with the reason, it is shown by `result_retirement_repairs`, retried every pass, and other custody keeps
retiring in the same pass; an unlink or fsync error keeps the row `retiring`, charged and retried. The context sweep finishes
context-only custody (custody released, no reservation row, or its own `retiring` / `repair_required` retry) with no
reservation row read or written, and never selects a context that has a reservation. Start-up reconciliation removes orphan
and partial context and body files and one name of a link pair using directory listing and `lstat` only: no body or context
bytes are read, and its work does not grow with the number of tombstones (RS-D-9). A 1 MiB body is returned through every
chunk (K2).
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-D.md draft 3 s4-s6, draft 4 s1, rows U1-U10, K1, K2, S1; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md SH-3 (retirement); docs/requirements/d3.md.

RS-D-D4.statement:
**RS-D-D4 — Publication material and replay.**
The prepare transaction stores the exact prepared material (the canonical bytes whose keyed digest is `prepared_digest`) in
`project_result_publications`; the commit transaction removes it, and so does the transaction that records `retiring`. A
failed publication with the service live is retried from the kept packet (the live lane keeps it until its own commit) and
commits once, reusing the final body file, with `prepared_digest` and `retained_until_ms` unchanged. A publication is committed
from the store, by a successor or by settlement arbitration, only while it is still eligible, decided inside the commit
transaction: the reservation is `reserved`, its RS-B obligation row is `held`, the context is `bound`, and the stored material
verifies (its digest, binding, assignment digest, terminal record, usage record and the final body's digest); no deadline is a
condition. An ineligible or altered publication is refused (`history_conflict` when altered) and only finishes cleanup. Before
the account is asked to settle an attempt the project writer arbitrates it: `recovered` (a verifiable body is committed
first), `unrecoverable` (the obligation row goes `releasing`, so no publication of that attempt, live or replayed, commits
afterwards) or `settling` (a `releasing` row or a settlement row already exists: nothing is committed, cleanup follows). A
stop before the body's final link leaves a run that RS-B's settlement ends lost, with no half-recorded state; a result is
lost only when the service stops before a verifiable final body exists (RS-D-12 as narrowed; no numeric bound, owner
decision 90.1 A and 90.2 A). A replay that commits a claim that has a live job is adopted by the lane once.
Source: DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-D.md draft 3 s1-s3, s6, draft 4 s2-s4, rows P1, R1-R6, R3', R4', P2', P3', X1-X3, L1-L3; DESIGN-0.4.0-RS-BD-shared.md S-2, S-3; docs/requirements/d4.md.

RS-S13-CONTROLS.statement: Regression controls: patching the product in the test only, to release 128 rows per call or to slow the reservation/hold JOIN by 6 ms, turns the per-batch and B1 checks red; the mechanism check is red for an unbounded selection or a missing back-off; a pass that drains everything clears the production finding.

RSA3-1.statement: **RSA3-1 — Outstanding owner preparation.** Decision 87 F6: a swept owner-API reservation whose prepare signature work is still running refuses its late return without faulting claims, forgets its handle and releases capacity once.

RSA3-2.statement: **RSA3-2 — Crashed-slot restore.** Decision 87 F5: back up and restore a project with a crashed or lost run_holds slot; consistency passes and slot accounting is preserved exactly.

RSA3-3.statement: **RSA3-3 — Late-completion comparison, test only.** ledger-local and account releases differ by design on a decided slot (RS-A-2, decision 106b).

RSA3-4.statement: **RSA3-4 — Release-batch query cost.** Every SQL statement run per release batch by account_holds_due and close_expired_reserved uses an index for its WHERE/ORDER; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on a real ledger shows no table scans.

RSA3-5.statement: **RSA3-5 — Release-batch rows unchanged.** The same seeded ledger selects the same due rows before and after the query-cost fix; account_holds_due agrees with _release_due_locked.

RSF-S2-1.statement:
**RSF-S2-1 — Exclusive lifetime ownership.** Both store owners acquire their
existing, protected writer flock before opening/migrating a database. A live
predecessor, including a stopped/paused executable, prevents adoption and new
admissions. Do not infer exit from a failed health check. Keep the same lock
inode/descriptor until the connection closes; refuse lost, replaced, unlinked,
inherited or released ownership, without reacquiring it. Never unlink locks.
A released lifetime lock proves the predecessor has retired its connection;
real executable tests additionally wait for process exit before migration.

RSF-S2-2.statement:
**RSF-S2-2 — Atomic epoch before adoption.** Each successful owner acquisition
advances one durable singleton `runtime_takeover` epoch, retaining the preceding
and current loaded runtime digest. Install it in the schema transaction before
any historical hold adoption; roll it back with a failed migration. A successor
opening the same build also advances the epoch. Publish no owner/admission
interface until initialization and validation succeed. Supported historical
records still upgrade through the existing authorization and backup gates.

RSF-S2-3.statement:
**RSF-S2-3 — Every current write.** A central connection boundary checks the
captured epoch and lifetime ownership inside every write transaction and again
before commit. Cover account/project admissions, direct writes, autocommit,
cursor/batch/script writes, explicit transactions, sweeps, backup registration,
deletion and VACUUM/journal maintenance. Transactional writes by a paused stale
writer must refuse with zero committed changes after takeover, even if it
retains a connection. VACUUM/journal-mode maintenance checks immediately before
and after the operation while retaining the lifetime flock. SQLite cannot wrap
these operations in the epoch transaction: a revocation during maintenance can
be detected afterwards but cannot undo its already durable changes.
Rollback and connection close must remain possible after revocation.

RSF-S2-4.statement:
**RSF-S2-4 — Exclude old executable reopen.** Advance ledger schema 16→17
and project schema 21→22 so genuine older executables cannot reopen either
migrated store, including an offline CLI. Test an unmodified git archive of
0.8.55 (`8d4a7ce3`) holding each store, racing migration, and retrying after
migration. Old stores are positive upgrade fixtures; old runtimes are negative
writer fixtures. Do not change VERSION or the runtime digest catalogue.

RSF-S2-5.statement:
**RSF-S2-5 — Plain refusals.** Current fencing refusals identify ownership or
runtime replacement in plain language and include the exact trusted command
`./setup.sh --update`. Keep existing busy/incompatible reason codes so wire
reason inventories do not grow. Already installed old binaries cannot acquire
new message text; their existing schema refusal is the negative fence proof.

RSF-S2-6.statement:
**RSF-S2-6 — Preservation and validation.** Preserve signed/historical records,
existing backup formats and project partitions. The machine-local epoch never
travels in a per-project learning backup or source image. Register new tests,
run them red before code then green, and prove `metadata_errors: []`. Run only
named modules, including every copier/backup/restore/move/enumeration module
affected by the schema step. Record evidence and unrun checks in
[STATUS.md](rsf-s2/STATUS.md). Existing assertions may change only with an
old→new entry in [assertions.md](rsf-s2/assertions.md).

RSF-S3-1.statement:
**RSF-S3-1 — Durable bounded progress.** Adopt historical account slots,
bindings and probes, and project leases, reservations, contexts, custody and
orchestrations by class, seeking a durable source cursor. Each adoption batch visits at
most 64 source rows. Its writes and cursor commit together. Resume skips
committed batches and retries an uncommitted batch. A migration whose entire
adoption fits in 64 source rows may retain one atomic transaction. Freeze
classification time across resumptions. Historical records remain upgradeable.
The first transaction's legacy backfills for account ledgers below 17 and the
final transaction's account release-due sweep and full account/project validators
are **not batch-bounded**. These transactions are atomic and idempotent on resume;
the 64-row bound applies to adoption, not to the entire upgrade.

RSF-S3-2.statement:
**RSF-S3-2 — Fence every batch.** Retain S2's lifetime writer lock and claim
the runtime_takeover epoch before adoption. Check ownership and epoch at each
batch transaction and commit. A dead owner releases its lock; a successor
claims a fresh epoch. Revocation must roll back the pending batch and cursor.
Preserve the authorization and verified backup gates on the original upgrade.
Exercise a real successor process after SIGKILL, assert its epoch increments on
resume, and prove a retained stale owner cannot commit adoption rows and cursor.

RSF-S3-3.statement:
**RSF-S3-3 — Validate before exposure.** Pending migration metadata prevents
ordinary startup from serving a partial register. Only an explicitly authorized
owner may resume it. Before the first durable batch, install the existing
target version to exclude old executables. This version is an exclusion fence,
not publication: remove the pending marker only with successful register,
custody and schema validation. Keep the original project pre-upgrade copy
through an interrupted migration. A failure before the first checkpoint keeps
the existing rollback behavior; after it, retain progress for retry.
Pending refusals give the plain next step and `Run: ./setup.sh --update`.
Reset the connection's temporary migration context even if adoption or validation
raises. Before resuming a project, require the kept before-copy named by the
original attempt marker; refuse plainly if that recovery copy is missing.

RSF-S3-4.statement:
**RSF-S3-4 — Process-death equivalence.** Use real subprocesses and SIGKILL
immediately before and after a batch commit, including a second interruption
after resume, the last short batch / `done=1` commit for every class, and the
publication commit containing progress-table removal after full validation.
Reopen twice and compare all historical identities, row counts,
signed/sealed bytes and adopted rows against an uninterrupted upgrade from
the same source. Verify durable cursors at the kill boundary, class coverage,
bounded batches, failed validation and revoked ownership.

RSF-S3-5.statement:
**RSF-S3-5 — Stable final formats.** Reuse ledger 17 and project 22. Temporary
progress metadata exists only during migration and disappears atomically on
publication; no permanent schema step, VERSION or runtime catalogue bump is
needed. Keep progress out of backups and source images by withholding the
owner until validation. Exercise the source-image reader and named copy,
backup, restore, move and record-enumeration modules. Register scenario tests
and prove `metadata_errors: []`. Record evidence and limitations in
[STATUS.md](rsf-s3/STATUS.md); pair any existing assertion edits in
[assertions.md](rsf-s3/assertions.md).

RSF-S6-1.statement:
**RSF-S6-1 — Orchestration.** Adopt open and paused sealed orchestrations as
held, with their original identity and activity-based due time. Preserve closed
orchestrations. Run classification inside S3's bounded, cursor-based migration
under S2's lifetime lock and epoch, including interruption and two reopens.

RSF-S6-2.statement:
**RSF-S6-2 — Open-binding duty.** Backfill missing pre-B3 duties from retained
host opens. Verify the original journal and lease before using their facts.
A bound lease has a claimed duty tombstone; an unresolved open stays held.
Retain the original run and attempt. If withdrawal inputs are absent, keep a
named evidence wait with a plain owner next step; never guess inputs or release
on a timer. Existing duties and authenticated replies remain unchanged. An
already recorded result proves its open duty fulfilled; preserve its register
without adding a duty.

Fix round MED-2: a verified historical open whose expired lease already has a
released `denied` or `fenced` tombstone uses that retained authenticated receipt
to release its backfilled duty as `fenced`, as the existing denial path does.
Prove this from a real schema-21 store, without inferring closure from expiry,
missing inputs or predecessor exit alone; preserve existing duties and receipts.
For a pre-B1 denial adopted without a receipt, the verified sealed expired lease
plus its verified host open and the existing B1 `denied` adoption predicate are
the retained no-launch evidence; preserve the absent receipt without inventing one.

RSF-S6-3.statement:
**RSF-S6-3 — Settlement.** Classify an unfinished historical reservation as
held awaiting account settlement, with a named reason and plain next step.
Run B4s publication arbitration before the account outbox; only its verified
closure releases the reservation as lost. In the report, lost maps to the
existing `abandoned` count; the reservation hold records release kind `lost`.
Preserve a completed result during arbitration. Replay remains stable.

RSF-S6-4.statement:
**RSF-S6-4 — Result custody.** Preserve finished result, terminal, sealed
context and historical record bytes. A verifiable committed result with its
stored inputs and open sealed orchestration remains recordable by the current
fenced service after upgrade, including after restart. Bind that permission to
this migrated attempt and the current owner runtime; an arbitrary runtime or an
ordinary fresh-store mismatch still refuses. Missing inputs remain
legacy_no_context with custody and an owner next step, without fabricated inputs.

RSF-S6-5.statement:
**RSF-S6-5 — Memory-only preparation.** Do not reconstruct driver or preparation
memory. Report those categories as tracked with zero invented historical holds (B2). Classify any surviving unarmed
lease as held with a named legacy preparation reason and plain owner next step;
no missing-memory inference releases an uncertain obligation. Pure memory with
no durable source creates no invented hold or launch authority.

Fix round MED-1/LOW-3: every new owner step names an existing CLI command or a
documented automatic release. Ordinary fresh-store runtime mismatch points to
the existing setup update command. Unarmed leases still release automatically
on the service's expiry sweep or when the successor releases unused leases;
pending claims require the account's authenticated no-launch evidence.

RSF-S6-6.statement:
**RSF-S6-6 — Late publication refusal.** The B4s releasing fence and verified
lost settlement each refuse a late publication with zero changes to terminal,
record, context, body or reservation state. Resume classification without
replacing existing duty/settlement evidence. Verify bounded batches and atomic
cursor rollback under real process death and a revoked S2 epoch.

Fix round LOW-1: both `publish_result` and `commit_result` must refuse with the
specific reason `history_result_expired` before and after lost settlement and
after reopen, with zero database or artifact changes.

RT-RX-1.statement:
### RT-RX-1 — One provider-state classifier

Routing snapshots, open admission, and the existing before-launch check shall derive usage state from the same classifier, with the same provider, account evidence and evaluation time. Its externally distinguishable states shall be `ample`, `constrained`, `exhausted`, and `unknown`. These are usage states, not admission verdicts or provider-configuration eligibility.

**Acceptance:** Identical evidence and time produce identical state in snapshot construction, open and launch; no second routing-only threshold, stale-reading rule, or optimistic state translation exists. An exhausted state produces `provider_exhausted` when earlier admission gates pass.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps open/launch's shared `headroom_state` use at `admission_metadata.py:284` and `admission_metadata.py:481`; changes the three-state/default-ample classifier at `admission_metadata.py:379` and the state-free route interface at `routing.py:1836`. Authority: 124.2; analysis lines 14–19.

RT-RX-10.statement:
### RT-RX-10 — Escalation remains meaningful after a usage switch

When the surviving selected setting is on the configured family ladder, keep existing failure qualification and escalation semantics: attempt 2 uses the next eligible higher rung when qualified, attempt 3 uses the strongest eligible higher rung, and no higher eligible rung retains the current surviving pick. Filter exhausted providers throughout. Do not silently disable an otherwise applicable escalation solely because the provider was switched for usage. A surviving setting absent from the ladder needs the explicit resolution in OPEN-4; no invented strength order is specified here.

**Acceptance:** A usage switch to an on-ladder setting still yields `next`, `strongest`, or `none_higher` according to the surviving ladder, with correct from/to settings. Unconfirmed judgment failures remain held and non-ladder families still do not escalate. A usage switch alone must not produce a misleading successful quality escalation or an unexplained `off_ladder`; the off-ladder fixture remains an explicit unresolved case until OPEN-4 is settled.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps failure qualification at `routing.py:1532`–`routing.py:1562` and rung semantics at `routing.py:1567`–`routing.py:1580`; addresses `off_ladder` at `routing.py:1563`. Authority: 124.3; analysis line 13.

RT-RX-11.statement:
### RT-RX-11 — Verifier selection keeps the other-provider preference

For a worker's actual selected provider, prefer the other eligible, non-exhausted provider, then the worker's own eligible, non-exhausted provider. Use the existing family/risk verifier model, effort and agent rules. Constrained/unknown state shall not demote a preferred verifier. Verification tasks for known work shall use this same rule with the actual worker provider and bound outcome, rather than reuse an obsolete advertised verifier blindly.

**Acceptance:** For both worker providers, every risk and supported family, a non-exhausted eligible other provider wins even if constrained/unknown. If it exhausts, the worker's provider is the fallback when eligible and non-exhausted. If neither is available, no verifier is invented. With unchanged state, advertised and actual verification routes agree on provider/model/effort; meaningful work still requires verification and verification does not recursively require verification.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps preference and risk settings at `routing.py:1473`/`routing.py:1489`, known-work selection at `routing.py:1608`, and verification requirement at `routing.py:1734`; extends `_select_verifier` at `routing.py:1458` with usage filtering. Authority: 124.1.

RT-RX-12.statement:
### RT-RX-12 — Same-provider verification is always non-independent

Whenever the verifier's actual provider equals its worker's actual provider, the advertised verifier and actual verification route shall explicitly record `independent=false`, regardless of family, risk, policy version or escalation scope. The marker shall survive a verifier re-pick. A different provider shall not acquire this false marker merely from a previous advertised fallback, and provider diversity alone shall not attest a completed independent verification verdict.

**Acceptance:** Cross-product assertions over both providers, all risks and all supported worker families find explicit false on every same-provider pair, including high/critical, default installations and families outside judgment scope. A re-pick from other-provider to same-provider becomes false. A re-pick back to a different provider does not retain false from the old route; execution/verdict audit remains unobserved until real evidence arrives.

**Keeps/changes:** Broadens conditional marking at `routing.py:1506`, scope checks at `routing.py:1618`/`routing.py:1744`, and actual-route projection at `routing.py:1822`; keeps route-versus-observation distinction at `routing.py:1810`. Authority: 124.4.

RT-RX-13.statement:
### RT-RX-13 — Re-pick the verifier at its own open

The worker route's verifier is a recommendation at that snapshot time. At the verifier's own open, obtain current trusted state and select the verifier again using the worker's actual provider, original verification family/risk, and bound worker outcome. If the advertised provider has become exhausted since the worker route, select the remaining eligible provider, apply RT-RX-12, and admit that actual verifier normally. Do not rerun, relabel or replace the completed worker to avoid this race.

**Acceptance:** A worker routed at t1 advertises the other provider; that provider exhausts before verification at t2. The verifier open chooses the eligible survivor with the correct verifier model/effort, records both recommendations and the reason for change, marks same-provider false, and keeps the same worker/outcome binding. If both exhaust at t2, verification is unsatisfied; a worker result alone is not recorded as verified.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps known-work route correspondence at `routing.py:1608`, risk selection at `routing.py:1617`, and final usage check at `admission_metadata.py:287`; changes reliance on the earlier advertisement at `routing.py:1737`. Authority: analysis line 12 and 124.1/124.4.

RT-RX-14.statement:
### RT-RX-14 — At most one exhaustion-triggered re-route at open

For each logical child open (worker or verifier), a fresh open denial whose reason is exactly `provider_exhausted` may cause one automatic refresh of the trusted snapshot, re-route, and alternative open. This is at most two open attempts total for that logical child, including across replay/recovery; it is not an unbounded provider ping-pong. The replacement still uses normal admission, account-wide run caps, task attempt limits and execution bounds. A second exhaustion denial terminates recovery with an explicit unsuccessful outcome; both exhausted uses RT-RX-16. Non-exhaustion denials do not trigger this mechanism.

**Acceptance:** A provider becoming exhausted between route and open causes zero launches there and at most one alternative open. Inject a second exhaustion denial: no third open occurs, including after a replay. A survivor at its cap returns `window_run_cap_reached` and is not launched or retried via another provider under this mechanism. Passing admissions are counted normally and never charged twice; denied opens do not create admitted runs. Keep logical task/parent/outcome lineage and link both attempts in audit. Durable retry ownership is OPEN-5.

**Keeps/changes:** Adds bounded recovery around `admission_metadata.py:287`; keeps account cap at `admission_metadata.py:289`, future-admission counting at `admission_metadata.py:296`, route bounds at `routing.py:1751`, and authoritative original-open evaluation at `account_open_admission.py:44`. Authority: analysis lines 14–15 and standing rule.

RT-RX-15.statement:
### RT-RX-15 — Admission and before-launch checks retain final authority

A non-exhausted route snapshot is advisory. Open shall still perform the full current admission sequence, and launch shall still perform its existing recheck. Preserve API-key refusal, identity/client/subscription checks, owner attestation, paid-usage/spend-control restrictions, billing freshness/bootstrap limits, run caps, signature/current-permission checks and atomic original-open behavior. Only the headroom classifier correction in 124.2 changes admission permission; reporting unknown separately does not deny an otherwise admitted unknown window.

**Acceptance:** A route selecting any provider cannot bypass each existing denial reason when independently injected. Exhaustion arriving after open still prevents launch. An unknown Codex window with valid remaining evidence still admits. API-key, paid usage, missing identity/attestation, billing and cap denials keep their existing priority and cannot be treated as exhaustion-triggered failover. Launch does not recount the admission cap.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps fixed-order gates at `admission_metadata.py:207`–`admission_metadata.py:307`, launch rules at `admission_metadata.py:431`–`admission_metadata.py:483`, and raw recapture/commit authority at `account_open_admission.py:3`; changes only RT-RX-1–5's headroom semantics. Authority: standing rule.

RT-RX-16.statement:
### RT-RX-16 — Structured result when both providers are exhausted

When both provider states are exhausted, return a structured, non-executable unsatisfied routing result instead of `ContractError`, for worker selection and verifier selection, including refresh/re-route paths. Its observable contract shall contain an unsatisfied discriminator, cause `provider_exhausted`, task identity, selection phase (worker/verifier), snapshot evaluation time/reference, and entries keyed by both `codex` and `claude`, each with state `exhausted`, account scope, deciding evidence/reason and next known reset or explicit null. Do not fill successful execution fields with a fake selected worker/verifier. Exact wire names/version are OPEN-6; these semantic fields are required.

**Acceptance:** Both exhausted yields an inspectable result naming both providers and their states, never either no-candidate exception. Known future reset times are surfaced; absent reset stays null, with fallback expiry separate. With multiple blocking explicit windows, the next known reset is the earliest future reset among the applicable blocking windows, not a guarantee that all restrictions end then; later blockers remain inspectable. Consumers stop without launch or a success/verified claim. A successful worker whose verifier is unsatisfied retains its worker result and an unsatisfied verification phase.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes usage-caused no-candidate behavior at `routing.py:1683` and `routing.py:1510`; extends successful-only output at `routing.py:1773`. Authority: 124.5; resolves the missing shape noted at analysis line 9 at the semantic level.

RT-RX-17.statement:
### RT-RX-17 — Bridge/configuration failure is a separate cause

Usage routing shall not turn on `codex_primary_may_bridge_to_claude` or bypass disabled providers, model allowlists, unavailable agents or bridged-write containment. With Codex exhausted and Claude not exhausted but blocked by the Codex-primary bridge flag, report the distinct bridge/configuration no-candidate cause, not “both exhausted.” Preserve existing policy-only `ContractError` behavior for invalid inputs and no eligible configured candidates; 124.5 does not authorize converting every error to exhaustion. If both states really are exhausted, RT-RX-16 applies and any additional policy exclusions remain separately visible.

**Acceptance:** With both providers enabled, bridge=false, Codex-primary and Codex exhausted/Claude ample, no Claude launch occurs and the diagnostic identifies the bridge prohibition separately from Codex exhaustion. Turning the flag on makes an otherwise eligible Claude candidate selectable. Disabling both providers with no exhausted evidence retains existing no-candidate refusal. Invalid primary/task/configuration still fails closed. Exact mixed-cause diagnostic representation is OPEN-6.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps bridge flag at `routing.py:1287`, provider/model allowlists at `routing.py:1271`, writable mapping exclusion at `routing.py:1666`, and policy-only no-candidate errors at `routing.py:1684`; adds distinct usage-versus-policy diagnostics. Authority: 124.1; analysis lines 12–13.

RT-RX-18.statement:
### RT-RX-18 — Availability audit coexists with v5 selection identity

Record a separately identifiable provider-availability audit alongside the existing selection audit: classifier/snapshot format identity, evaluation time and snapshot reference, per-provider account/state/evidence/reset/fallback expiry, candidates considered in policy order and their skip causes, actual worker/verifier choice, usage-driven switch, and re-route count/trigger with original and replacement open references. Preserve policy/configuration/mapping digests and existing risk/escalation/failure lineage. For unopted v6 cells, keep `selection.policy_version=5` and the existing selection identity; do not relabel those cells v6 or conflate availability with policy/model selection.

**Acceptance:** Audit reconstructs why a worker/verifier skipped each provider and distinguishes `unknown` from `ample`, usage from bridge exclusion, quality escalation from usage switch, and initial route from open recovery. For an unaffected unopted cell, the legacy selection subtree is identical and its policy version remains 5; added availability data lives outside that subtree. Requested settings remain distinct from observed execution and verdicts. Same-provider marking required by 124.4 is still present even when it changes the full route serialization.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps explicit v5 identity at `routing.py:1754`–`routing.py:1760`, provider config digest at `routing.py:1792`, mapping digest at `routing.py:1824`, and observed/verdict placeholders at `routing.py:1809`–`routing.py:1815`; adds availability audit outside `_selection_metadata` use at `routing.py:1753`. Authority: analysis line 10, 124.2/124.4/124.5.

RT-RX-19.statement:
### RT-RX-19 — Evidence remains attributable and bounded

The snapshot/audit shall reference trusted identity and deciding headroom/billing evidence, plus the later clearing reading when it supersedes resetless evidence. Evidence from another project may decide account state, but shall retain its owning-project provenance; do not falsely present foreign references as locally held admission evidence. Preserve bounded admission evidence and existing project-local citation filtering. A Codex billing-only exhaustion must have an attributable billing reason/reference even if no headroom digest exists. Do not expose raw account identifiers or authentication secrets.

**Acceptance:** Cross-project exhaustion and clearing are reproducible using resolvable, scoped snapshot evidence, while stored admission citations remain a subset of that project's held records. A large history does not produce an unbounded list of admission digests. Billing-only exhaustion is explainable without a fabricated headroom reference; unknown does not cite imaginary favorable evidence. Raw provider credentials/identity values do not appear in routing audit. Snapshot size limits are OPEN-3.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps evidence intersection at `admission_metadata.py:200`, bounded deciding-level intent at `admission_metadata.py:388`, and local citation construction at `account_open_admission.py:29`; addresses billing-only state without a headroom digest at `admission_metadata.py:413`–`admission_metadata.py:418`. Authority: standing admission rule and analysis lines 11/14.

RT-RX-2.statement:
### RT-RX-2 — State boundaries and unknown evidence

A live numeric window at or above 90% exhausts either provider; 75% through below 90% is constrained; usable live numeric readings below 75% are ample in the absence of a stronger applicable restriction. Claude `rejected` exhausts and `allowed_warning` constrains even for an empty windows collection, subject to RT-RX-3–5. The most restrictive applicable evidence wins except for the expressly authorized supersession. Missing Codex windows, all-null utilization, or only expired usage evidence shall be reported as unknown when no other applicable evidence establishes a state. Unknown shall not be invented as ample, shall not cause a usage skip, and shall pass the headroom gate at open; other admission gates still apply. Keep the current Codex `ordinary_usage_allowed=false` exhaustion rule separately identifiable as a billing-derived usage restriction.

**Acceptance:** Both providers classify numeric 74.99/75/89.99/90 as ample/constrained/constrained/exhausted; either a second live 90% window or Claude rejection dominates a low numeric reading. A Codex account with no usable window is `known: false` ("unknown") in the route snapshot, remains a routing candidate, is still rated ample by admission's headroom_state, and is admitted with otherwise passing evidence. Codex ordinary-usage denial remains exhausted, including the existing future-evidence case. Partial numeric coverage and Claude allowed-without-utilization are OPEN-2.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps thresholds/status precedence at `admission_metadata.py:29`, `admission_metadata.py:64`, and billing exhaustion at `admission_metadata.py:407`. KEEPS admission's three-value rating vocabulary (exhausted/constrained/ample) and its ample default for absent or expired evidence (`admission_metadata.py:88`, `:395`) unchanged (primary 2026-11-24: no new stored or returned rating value; shrinking/expanding validated vocabularies breaks real-ledger upgrades). "Unknown" exists only in the route's provider-state snapshot, as `known: false` for a provider with no applicable evidence, and in the route audit. Authority: 124.1 and standing rule.

RT-RX-20.statement:
### RT-RX-20 — Collection, compaction and replays preserve the classifier's answer

Evidence retention/merge/capture must preserve enough trusted later favorable evidence to implement 124.2; a collector that drops every favorable reading after a rejection cannot satisfy it. Compaction, cross-project capture, overflow, restart or replay shall neither resurrect a superseded resetless restriction nor drop an explicit live/future-stamped restriction. Preserve billing restrictions and cap accounting independently. No requirement here authorizes a new arbitrary observation append or weakens evidence authenticity.

**Acceptance:** The same sequence of resetless restrictive then later non-restrictive readings yields the same state before and after overflow/merge/capture/restart; explicit unreset and rollback cases stay restrictive through the same operations. Replay does not duplicate run admissions or restart the RT-RX-14 retry allowance. Existing bounded histories still work. Retention changes must be limited to evidence needed for the new classifier; the exact storage design remains implementation work.

**Keeps/changes:** Extends the account-wide evidence contract at `admission_metadata.py:178` and `account_open_admission.py:24`; changes the old unconditional restrictive-wins assumption at `admission_metadata.py:170`. Existing retention behavior is exposed by `test_providers.py:1398` and `test_providers.py:2608`; those behaviors cannot silently defeat 124.2. Authority: 124.2 and standing rule.

RT-RX-21.statement:
### RT-RX-21 — Preserve named regression behavior, with explicit authorized exceptions

The regression inventory below shall remain the preservation baseline. Tests whose assertions conflict directly with 124.2/124.4 or additive availability audit must be identified for narrow future revision, not cited as evidence that the owner decision can be ignored. This step does not edit tests, fixtures or golden files.

**Acceptance:** A later implementation's validation report names these existing tests, preserves unaffected assertions, and accounts explicitly for each changed assertion under RT-RX-1–20. No blanket golden regeneration hides unrelated provider/model/effort/risk/bounds/lineage changes. Existing no-candidate configuration errors remain covered separately from new both-exhausted results.

**Keeps/changes:** Keeps the behaviors exercised at the file:line locations below; permits only the exceptions stated below. Especially preserve `routing.py:1603` and `routing.py:1759`, while applying 124.2/124.4 to their affected outputs.

RT-RX-3.statement:
### RT-RX-3 — A later non-restrictive reading clears a resetless restriction

For the same provider and account, a restrictive headroom reading with no reset time, including an empty-window Claude rejection/warning or a restrictive window with `resets_at=null`, shall cease contributing its restriction when superseded by a later trusted non-restrictive reading. Do not require that reading to originate in the same project, run, or probe. This exception shall not clear an independent explicit unreset window or billing/paid-usage restriction. Mixed readings must retain any explicit unreset restrictive component.

**Acceptance:** A resetless 95% reading at t1 followed by a trusted 10% reading at t2, with t1 < t2 <= evaluation time, no longer exhausts; an empty-window Claude rejection followed by a later allowed 10% reading similarly clears. A reading for another account/provider or an older favorable reading does not clear. A separate explicit live 95% window still exhausts. Assert identical outcomes at route, open, and launch. Chronology ties and the complete meaning of non-restrictive are OPEN-1/2.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes unconditional restrictive-wins at `admission_metadata.py:170` and `admission_metadata.py:397`; keeps provider/account filtering at `admission_metadata.py:400`. Authority: 124.2; analysis lines 16–19.

RT-RX-4.statement:
### RT-RX-4 — Resetless headroom lasts five hours, not a day

Without a superseding reading, a resetless restrictive headroom reading shall expire after five hours from its observation time, including an empty-window status-only reading. Keep the existing inclusive age-bound convention: it still restricts at exactly five hours and expires at five hours plus one millisecond. The 24-hour horizon for paid usage and spend control shall remain unchanged. Do not manufacture a provider reset timestamp from this fallback expiry.

**Acceptance:** At ages five hours minus one millisecond, five hours, and five hours plus one millisecond, a resetless rejection/95% reading is restrictive, restrictive, then no longer restrictive. With no usable remaining reading the usage state is unknown, not ample. Paid-usage and spend-control evidence six hours old still denies under their existing rules. Audit distinguishes fallback expiry from a measured reset.

**Keeps/changes:** Changes resetless lifetime at `admission_metadata.py:55` and `admission_metadata.py:75`; keeps five-hour constant at `admission_metadata.py:38`, age comparison convention at `admission_metadata.py:61`, and billing horizons at `admission_metadata.py:328` and `admission_metadata.py:349`. Authority: 124.2.

RT-RX-5.statement:
### RT-RX-5 — Explicit resets and rollback protection

An explicit restrictive window with `resets_at > evaluation_time` shall remain restrictive despite a later favorable reading, until that reset, except a proven early reset (USAGE-RECHECK-3, decision 134 A). At the reset it no longer contributes. An expired explicit window shall not acquire a fresh resetless lifetime. A future-stamped restrictive observation shall not disappear merely because the evaluation clock moved backward; an older favorable reading cannot clear it.

**Acceptance:** Except a proven early reset (USAGE-RECHECK-3, decision 134 A), at reset minus one millisecond an explicit 95% window still exhausts despite a later 10% reading; at reset it does not. The same assertions apply to an explicit Claude rejected window. The trusted snapshot builder shall supply the route's account scope separately for Codex and Claude. Missing identity shall remain distinguishable from a known account with unknown usage and shall not become admission permission.

**Acceptance:** Exhaustion for account A does not exhaust account B; exhaustion for A in another project does affect A. Switching the trusted current identity from A to B changes the snapshot's scope and records its identity evidence. An arbitrary task fingerprint cannot select B or clear A. Missing/stale identity still fails open's identity gate; a valid identity with no usage passes only the usage gate. Account changes between snapshot and open require current admission, never reuse of A's state as B's.

RT-RX-7.statement:
### RT-RX-7 — Trusted route input with time and evidence

Live routing shall receive a trusted provider-state snapshot built with RT-RX-1, separate from task data and from the existing task-shape `trusted_routing_evidence_refs`. The snapshot shall identify its evaluation time, project/context binding, each provider and selected account fingerprint (or explicitly unavailable identity), identity evidence, usage state, deciding evidence references, reasons, known reset information and fallback expiry where applicable. Equal inputs and evaluation time shall produce deterministic results. A supplied state label alone is not trusted evidence. Snapshot transport, validation limits and freshness policy are OPEN-3.

**Acceptance:** A live route's recorded states and references match the builder's classification at the recorded time. Injecting an exhausted/ample label, fingerprint or evidence reference through task JSON cannot alter availability. A snapshot from another context cannot be treated as the current trusted snapshot. The snapshot grants no launch/admission authority. Offline behavior must explicitly distinguish unavailable live state; it must not claim ample (OPEN-3).

RT-RX-8.statement:
### RT-RX-8 — Worker selection preserves policy order

Within the existing eligible provider/model/agent candidates, select the first policy-ordered candidate whose provider is not exhausted. Do not rank ample ahead of constrained or unknown, insert an unconfigured provider, change risk cells, or change model/effort merely because utilization differs below 90%. Usage skips are additional to existing configuration, allowlist, mapping and containment exclusions. The standing rule to continue on the other provider applies when that provider has an eligible candidate.

**Acceptance:** For each policy order and both primary providers, the first eligible candidate wins with ample/constrained/unknown states in any combination. At 90% the exhausted first provider is skipped and the next eligible provider wins with its existing model/effort/agent/dispatch. At 89.99% it is not skipped. RT-RX-9.statement:

Every retry/escalation candidate shall pass the same exhaustion filter as the first worker pick. No ladder step, risk floor, legacy model fallback, or retry may restore an exhausted provider. A usage-driven provider switch shall not itself create a failed attempt, a semantic failure, evidence of independent verification, or entitlement to an additional attempt.

TF-18.statement:
**TF-18 — Normal sampling and soak separation.** Normal crash runs include an in-memory disk model
with separate volatile and durable file-content, mode and namespace states. Writes change volatile file
contents; create/unlink/rename/exchange/mkdir/rmdir change volatile namespace links. A file flush persists

implicitly an unflushed child's contents. SQLite commit state is tracked separately. Crash discards volatile
state and exposes only durable contents reachable through durable namespace links; recovery is then checked
against the single ML invariant and table. Permitted outcomes include complete S or T according to the
durable row, preserved owner objects and named unrecorded directories; torn published contents, lost
owner edits and a history direction inconsistent with recovered contents are rejected.
Witnesses distinguish flushed from unflushed writes, creates and renames, including flushing only one
rename parent; a missing production flush must change the model's post-crash outcome and fail the check.

phase, before/after side and commit label where applicable, plus stable occurrence/reproducer. Validate it
against discovered persistence-significant calls; every operation kind and relevant boundary needs a normal
sample. Normal selection includes the model and ci-profile generated cases, excluding complete sweeps.
Complete crash/fault sweeps, including recovery faults, run only under explicit `--profile soak` in
local-routing; soak includes the complete inventory, not merely persistence samples. Reject explicit soak

USAGE-RECHECK-1.statement:
### USAGE-RECHECK-1 - When a re-check is due

For each provider the classifier reports `recheck_due_at_ms`: when the state is `exhausted` and its
`next_reset_ms` is null or more than `USAGE_RECHECK_FAR_RESET_MS` after the evaluation time, it is the newest
usage reading of that provider/account (`observed_at_ms`, at or before evaluation time) plus
`USAGE_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS`; otherwise null. A re-check is due when `recheck_due_at_ms <= evaluation time`.
**Acceptance:** exhausted with a reset 3 days away and the newest reading 61 min old -> due; 10 min old -> not due
(due at reading + 60 min); exhausted with a reset 30 min away -> null; ample/constrained/unknown -> null.

USAGE-RECHECK-2.statement:
### USAGE-RECHECK-2 - The re-check reading itself

Codex re-checks with the existing non-spending observation (`account/rateLimits/read`). Claude re-checks with one
billing probe: while a re-check is due (USAGE-RECHECK-1), the probe's admission does not apply the exhausted gate;
every other probe gate stays (attestation, paid usage, API keys, managed config, cooldown, reuse). When no
re-check is due the exhausted gate still refuses the probe (keeps `test_bridge.py`
`test_exhausted_window_blocks_probes_at_ninety_percent`). A probe is not a run: no work, no run cap.
Cost (flag for owner): one Haiku low-effort single turn per re-check, at most one per provider per interval.
**Acceptance (real account service):** Claude exhausted (rejected, reset 3 days away) by a reading 61 min old ->
`provider-observe --provider claude --billing-probe` launches one probe and stores its records; same with a
reading 10 min old -> refused `provider_exhausted`, nothing launched.

USAGE-RECHECK-3.statement:
### USAGE-RECHECK-3 - An early reset clears a measured restriction (owner decision 134 (a): option A; changes RT-RX-5 only for a proven early reset)

A later reading (strictly later `observed_at_ms`, at or before evaluation time) of the same provider, account and
window (same `scope` and `window_minutes`, at least one of them known; review r1) that rates that window non-restrictive AND carries its own explicit
`resets_at` (the one that reading reported, never one a merge lent it) different from the restrictive window's proves the window reset early: it supersedes that window's
restriction (and a Claude `rejected` status bound to that window). This applies only while the restrictive
window's reset is more than `USAGE_RECHECK_FAR_RESET_MS` away at the clearing reading's time (a proof then stands as the old reset nears): a near reset is waited for, so RT-RX-5 and
`tests/test_providers.py:1171-1173` ("a later, favourable read does not clear a window that has not reset", reset
5 s away) are unchanged. A later reading with no reset time, for another
window, for another account, or older/equal in time does not clear it; RT-RX-5 is otherwise unchanged.
**Acceptance:** Claude `rejected` seven_day window (reset +3 days) at t1, later `allowed` seven_day 2% (reset +7
days) at t2 -> not exhausted; later five_hour-only reading -> still exhausted; later resetless reading -> still
exhausted (existing RT-RX-5 test); same for Codex 95% -> 10% on the same window with a new reset.
Option B if the live reading after an early reset keeps the old reset time: any later measured non-restrictive
reading of the same window supersedes it (changes `test_route_exhausted.py:84`).

USAGE-RECHECK-4.statement:
### USAGE-RECHECK-4 - Who triggers it (a) The primary host's route (`learning-route`, and the route re-pick at `learning-open-host-run`): when the snapshot says a re-check is due for a provider, take that one reading (USAGE-RECHECK-2), then re-read the snapshot and route on it. (b) Explicit: `provider-observe --provider

` (Codex) / `--billing-probe` (Claude) from the host is the re-check command. (c) The owner's `learning-status` shows each provider's state, `next_reset` and `recheck_due_at`; it takes no spending reading (the owner terminal cannot run probes, `tests/test_owner_terminal_flow.py:66`). **Acceptance (real account service):** route with Claude due -> exactly one probe; early-reset reading -> route may pick Claude; still rejected -> Claude skipped as today; a second route straight after -> no second probe.

USAGE-RECHECK-5.statement:
### USAGE-RECHECK-5 - Bounded, recorded, never real work on the exhausted provider

Selection uses only the snapshot read after the re-check; no worker or verifier is ever routed to a provider that
snapshot still calls exhausted. At most one re-check per provider per route call, and at most one per provider per
`USAGE_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS` across calls (the newest stored reading or reserved attempt is the clock, so a restart does not reset it; review r1: an attempt is reserved before any I/O and counts whether it yields a reading, no reading or a failure).
A re-check never fails the route: a refused or failed re-check routes on the existing snapshot. The route's
availability audit records `recheck: {<provider>: {"outcome": "cleared"|"still_exhausted"|"failed:<reason>",
"observed_at_ms": int|null}}` (`observed_at_ms`: the account's new reading, null when none arrived; `cleared` needs one); the probe's records are stored as every probe's are.
